translations.idiomatic: Treatise 58

sentences.zh: 郊社儀制郊社配饗祈穀雩祀天神太歲朝日夕月

translations.literal: Suburban Altar Rites; suburban altar collateral offerings; prayer for grain; rain sacrifice; worship of the celestial spirits; Grand Year; Morning Sun; Evening Moon
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altar rites; collateral offerings at the suburban altars; prayers for grain; rain sacrifices; worship of Heaven; the Grand Year; the Morning Sun; the Evening Moon

sentences.zh: 社稷先農先蠶地祇岳鎮海瀆山川直省神祇

translations.literal: State Altars; Spirit of the Soil and Grain; Spirit of the First Farmer; Spirit of the First Silkworm; earth spirits; mountains, peaks, seas, and rivers; mountains, rivers, and deities of each province
translations.idiomatic: The State Altars; the Spirit of the Soil and Grain; the Spirit of the First Farmer; the Spirit of the First Silkworm; earth spirits; the Five Sacred Peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and great rivers; and the mountain, river, and local deities of each province

sentences.zh: 郊祀之制太祖御極，焚香告天，建元天命。

translations.literal: On the institution of suburban sacrifice: When Taizu assumed the throne, he burned incense to announce to Heaven and established the reign title Destiny Bestowed by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On suburban sacrifice: When the Taizu Emperor took the throne, he burned incense to report to Heaven and proclaimed the reign era Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天聰十年，設圜丘德盛門外，方澤內治門外，壇壝始備。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tiancong, the Round Mound Altar was set up outside the Desheng Gate and the Square Pond Altar outside the Neizhi Gate, and the altar enclosures were first completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tiancong, the Round Mound was established outside the Desheng Gate and the Square Pond outside the Neizhi Gate, and the altar precincts were first put in order.

sentences.zh: 會征服察哈爾，獲元玉璽，躬親告祭，遂祀天南郊。

translations.literal: Upon the campaign to conquer Chahar, he obtained the Yuan jade seal; he personally performed the announcement sacrifice, and then sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: When the conquest of Chahar was completed and the Yuan jade seal was taken, he personally offered the announcement sacrifice and then performed the southern suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 舊制，祭饗用生牢，頒百官胙肉。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, sacrificial feasts used live victims, and sacrificial meat was distributed to all officials.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former practice, offerings at sacrifices used live animals, and sacrificial meat was issued to the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以天胙而享於家，是褻也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "To take Heaven's portion and enjoy it at home is profanation."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "To take what Heaven has granted and feast on it at home is to profane the rite."

sentences.zh: 諭改神前分享用熟薦。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that sharing before the spirits use cooked offerings instead.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that the portion shared before the spirits be changed to cooked offerings.

sentences.zh: 尋征朝鮮，祭告天地，並祀北郊。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, on the campaign against Korea, he announced the matter to Heaven and Earth and also sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, when setting out against Korea, he reported to Heaven and Earth and also sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關宅帝位，於是冬至祀圜丘，奉日、月、星辰、雲、雨、風、雷配。

translations.literal: When Shizu entered the Pass and took the imperial throne, at the winter solstice he sacrificed at the Round Mound, with the sun, moon, stars, clouds, rain, wind, and thunder as collateral spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor entered the Pass and assumed the throne, at the winter solstice he sacrificed at the Round Mound, with the sun, moon, stars, clouds, rain, wind, and thunder as accompanying spirits.

sentences.zh: 夏至祀方澤，奉岳、鎮、海、瀆配。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice he sacrificed at the Square Pond, with the peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and great rivers as collateral spirits.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice he sacrificed at the Square Pond, with the Five Peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and great rivers as accompanying spirits.

sentences.zh: 南北分饗。

translations.literal: Southern and northern sacrifices were held separately.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the southern and northern suburbs were kept distinct.

sentences.zh: 著為例。

translations.literal: This was established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This was fixed as precedent.

sentences.zh: 四年，定郊祀薦生牢如初，惟躬祀南郊進胙牛一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, suburban sacrifice was again fixed to use live victims as at first, but when the emperor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb only one ox of sacrificial meat was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, suburban offerings were again set to use live victims as before, but when the emperor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb only one presentation ox was advanced.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔言：「人君事天如父，歲止一郊，心有未盡。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict stated: "A ruler serves Heaven as a father; to sacrifice at the suburbs only once a year leaves the heart unsatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, an edict said, "The ruler serves Heaven as a father; to offer suburban sacrifice only once a year does not fully satisfy devotion.

sentences.zh: 惟營殿禁中，歲時致祀，配以太祖、太宗，庶昭誠敬。」

translations.literal: Only by building a hall within the palace precinct and offering seasonal sacrifices there, with Taizu and Taizong as collateral spirits, may sincerity and reverence be made manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Let a hall be built within the Forbidden City where seasonal offerings are made, with Taizu and Taizong as accompanying spirits, so that sincerity and reverence may be displayed."

sentences.zh: 禮臣乃援唐天寶四時孟月擇吉祭上帝故事，謂構上帝殿奉先殿東，元旦，萬壽，三節，夏冬二至，親詣致虔，儀物如郊祀。

translations.literal: The ritual officials then cited the Tang story of Tianbao, in which in each of the four seasons of the first month an auspicious day was chosen to sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, and proposed building a Hall of the Supreme Lord east of the Hall for Honoring Ancestors; on New Year's Day, the imperial birthday, the three festivals, and the summer and winter solstices the emperor would go in person with the same ritual objects as at suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials then cited the Tang Tianbao precedent of choosing an auspicious day in the first month of each season to sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, and proposed erecting a Hall of the Supreme Lord east of the Hall for Honoring Ancestors; on New Year's Day, the imperial birthday, the three great festivals, and the summer and winter solstices the emperor would attend in person, with ritual objects like those of suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 惟內祭初安神位時讀祝辭，不用胙，不進酒，不燎牛。

translations.literal: Only at the first installation of the spirit tablet in the inner sacrifice were the prayer text read aloud; no sacrificial meat, no wine offering, and no ox burned.
translations.idiomatic: For the inner sacrifice, only when the spirit tablet was first installed was the prayer read aloud; no sacrificial meat, no wine, and no ox were burned.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 至是始有禁中祀天禮。

translations.literal: From this time there was the rite of sacrificing to Heaven within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: From this point there was the palace rite of sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 十七年，敕廷臣議合祭儀，奏言仿明會典，前期一日，祭告各壇廟，定從祀十二壇。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the emperor commanded the court officials to deliberate on the rites of the combined sacrifice; they memorialized, following the Ming statutory compilation, that one day before the rite each altar and temple should be announced, and twelve altars were fixed for collateral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the emperor ordered the court to discuss the combined sacrifice; they reported, following the Ming Collected Statutes, that on the day before, announcement sacrifices should be made at each altar and temple, and twelve altars were designated for collateral worship.

sentences.zh: 是歲四月，禁中大饗殿遂合祀天、地、日、月暨諸神。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, the Grand Offeringing Hall in the palace then combined sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, sun, moon, and the various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fourth month, the Grand Offeringing Hall within the palace performed a combined sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, the sun, the moon, and the various spirits.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嗣位，詔罷之。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor succeeded to the throne, he ordered it abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sage Ancestor succeeded to the throne, he ordered this practice discontinued.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，定郊祀躬親行禮，無故不攝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, it was fixed that the emperor should personally perform suburban sacrifice and should not be represented except for cause.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, it was ordained that suburban sacrifice should be performed by the emperor in person and should not be delegated without good reason.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，冬至大祀，會天寒，群臣以代請，勿許。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, at the great winter solstice sacrifice, the weather was bitterly cold and the officials asked that a substitute perform; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, at the great winter solstice sacrifice the weather was severely cold; the officials asked that a substitute perform, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，帝違和，始令李光地攝行郊壇大禮。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year the emperor fell ill and first ordered Li Guangdi to perform the great suburban rites as substitute.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year, when the emperor was unwell, he first ordered Li Guangdi to perform the great suburban rites by proxy.

sentences.zh: 越二年，祀圜丘如初。

translations.literal: Two years later, sacrifice at the Round Mound resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, sacrifice at the Round Mound was again conducted as before.

sentences.zh: 嗣是帝年逾六十，兼病足，復令大臣攝之。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when the emperor passed sixty and also suffered from foot ailment, he again had great ministers perform by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: After this, when the emperor passed sixty and also suffered from foot trouble, he again had great ministers act as proxy.

sentences.zh: 明年冬至，齋戒，猶力疾升壇省俎豆，量力拜跽，退處幄次，俟攝事者禮訖始還宮。

translations.literal: The next year at the winter solstice, though observing abstention he still forced himself to ascend the altar to inspect the offerings, bowing and kneeling as his strength allowed; he withdrew to the tent and only returned to the palace after the proxy had finished the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter solstice, though keeping abstention, he still forced himself to ascend the altar to inspect the offerings, bowing and kneeling as his strength allowed; he withdrew to the tent and returned to the palace only after the proxy had completed the rite.

sentences.zh: 臣工固請停躬詣，猶勿許。

translations.literal: The officials repeatedly asked that he cease attending in person, but this was still not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The officials repeatedly begged him to stop attending in person, but this too was refused.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，祀南郊，始遣世宗恭代，距賓天止五日也。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, at sacrifice at the southern suburb, he first sent the Shizong Emperor respectfully to substitute; this was only five days before his death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year, at the southern suburban sacrifice, he first sent the Shizong Emperor to substitute in all reverence—only five days before his death.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年冬至，遇聖祖忌日，禮臣援舊例請代，下大學士九卿議。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of the eighth year of Yongzheng, it fell on the Sage Ancestor's death anniversary; the ritual officials cited precedent and asked for a substitute, and the matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of the eighth year of Yongzheng, which coincided with the Sage Ancestor's death anniversary, the ritual officials cited precedent and asked for a substitute; the matter was sent to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers for discussion.

sentences.zh: 奏言周禮春官稱大祭祀王不親則攝行。

translations.literal: They reported that the Zhou Rites, Office of Spring, states that at great sacrifices, if the king does not attend, another performs by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: They reported that the Zhou Rites, Office of Spring, says that at great sacrifices, if the king does not attend in person, another performs by proxy.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋制，大祀與國忌同日，樂備不作。

translations.literal: Under Tang and Song regulations, when a great sacrifice fell on the same day as a state mourning anniversary, music was prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang and Song practice, when a great sacrifice fell on the same day as a state mourning anniversary, music was prepared but not played.

sentences.zh: 議者謂饗神不可無樂，未若攝祀之當乎禮也，遣代便。

translations.literal: Deliberators held that to feast the spirits without music was improper, and that proxy sacrifice was more in accord with ritual; delegation was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Discussants held that to feast the spirits without music was not right, whereas proxy sacrifice accorded better with ritual; delegation was approved.

sentences.zh: 可其奏。

translations.literal: Their memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Their report was approved.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，定議周禮祀天用玉輅，唐、宋參用大輦，今親祀南郊，前期詣齋宮，宜御玉輦。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong, deliberation fixed that the Zhou Rites prescribe the jade chariot for sacrificing to Heaven, while Tang and Song also used the great carriage; for the present, when the emperor personally sacrifices at the southern suburb and beforehand goes to the abstention palace, he should ride the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong, deliberation established that the Zhou Rites prescribe the jade chariot for sacrifice to Heaven, while Tang and Song also used the great carriage; for the present, when the emperor personally sacrifices at the southern suburb and beforehand goes to the abstention palace, he should ride the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝乘禮輿，易鑾輅，自降輦至禮成，如儀。

translations.literal: On that day the emperor rode the ritual carriage, changed to the imperial carriage, and from dismounting the carriage until the rite was completed, all proceeded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor rode the ritual carriage, then changed to the imperial carriage; from dismounting until the rite was finished, all proceeded according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 十四年，展拓兩郊壇宇，更新幄次。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the precincts of the two suburban altars were expanded and the ritual tents renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the precincts of the two suburban altars were enlarged and the ritual tents renewed.

sentences.zh: 越四載蕆事，規制始大備。

translations.literal: Four years later the work was completed, and the regulations were then fully in place.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later the work was completed, and the system was then fully established.

sentences.zh: 仁宗中葉，自製南北郊說，祀典如故。

translations.literal: In the middle years of the Renzong reign, he himself composed expositions on the southern and northern suburbs, but the sacrificial canon remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle years of Renzong, he himself wrote treatises on the southern and northern suburbs, but the sacrificial canon remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年、九年，帝疾不能親，猶宮內致齋，屆日詣大高殿皇穹宇行禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth and ninth years of Xianfeng, the emperor was too ill to attend in person, yet still kept abstention within the palace; on the day he went to the Dagao Hall and the Imperial Vault of Heaven to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth and ninth years of Xianfeng, the emperor was too ill to attend in person, yet still kept abstention within the palace and on the appointed day went to the Dagao Hall and the Imperial Vault of Heaven to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 穆宗、德宗，沖齡踐阼，皆遣代。

translations.literal: Muzong and Dezong, ascending the throne in tender years, all sent substitutes.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong and Dezong, who took the throne as children, all sent substitutes.

sentences.zh: 定親政日躬行。

translations.literal: It was fixed that on the day of assuming personal rule they should perform in person.
translations.idiomatic: It was ordained that on the day they assumed personal rule they should perform the rite in person.

sentences.zh: 宣統纘緒，監國攝政王行之。

translations.literal: When Xuantong continued the succession, the regent performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuantong continued the line, the regent performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 郊社之儀，天聰十年，禮部進儀注，迄順治間，始定郊祀前期齋戒閱祝版玉帛香，省牲，祀日遲明，禮部太常官詣皇穹宇行禮。

translations.literal: As for the rites of the suburban altars, in the tenth year of Tiancong the Board of Rites submitted the ritual protocol; only in the Shunzhi period were fixed the preliminaries for suburban sacrifice—abstention, inspection of prayer boards, jade, silk, and incense, inspection of victims—and on the day of sacrifice, at dawn, Board of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials went to the Imperial Vault of Heaven to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding suburban altar rites: in the tenth year of Tiancong the Board of Rites submitted ritual protocols; only in the Shunzhi reign were fixed the preliminaries for suburban sacrifice—abstention, inspection of prayer boards, jade, silk, and incense, and inspection of victims—and on the sacrifice day, at dawn, Board of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials proceeded to the Imperial Vault of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 奉神牌置壇所，司祝奉祝版，帝出宮乘輦，陪祀王公集午門金水橋從行，餘序立橋南迎送。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets were placed at the altar; the prayer reader bore the prayer board; the emperor left the palace in his carriage; collateral-sacrifice princes and dukes assembled at the Jinshui Bridge of the Meridian Gate and followed; the rest took their places south of the bridge to welcome and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets were set on the altar; the prayer reader bore the prayer board; the emperor left the palace by carriage; princes and dukes joining the collateral sacrifice assembled at the Jinshui Bridge of the Meridian Gate and followed; the others stood south of the bridge to welcome and escort.

sentences.zh: 駕至昭亨門降輦，前引大臣十人，次贊引官、對引官導入更衣幄次，更祭服出，訖盥，詣二成拜位前，分獻官各就位。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession reached the Zhaohang Gate he dismounted; ten great ministers led in front, then the usher and counterpart officials guided him into the tent to change ritual dress; after washing he went to the bowing place on the second terrace; collateral-offering officials each took position.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession reached Zhaohang Gate the emperor dismounted; ten leading great ministers went before, then usher and counterpart officials guided him into the tent to change ritual dress; after ablutions he went to the bowing place on the second terrace, and collateral-offering officials each took their stations.

sentences.zh: 典儀贊「迎神燔柴」，司樂官贊「舉迎神樂」，贊引奏「升壇」，帝升一成。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies intoned "Welcome the spirits and burn the firewood"; the music master intoned "Play the music welcoming the spirits"; the usher played "Ascend the altar," and the emperor ascended the first terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies intoned, "Welcome the spirits and burn the firewood"; the music master intoned, "Play the music welcoming the spirits"; the usher struck up "Ascend the altar," and the emperor ascended the first terrace.

sentences.zh: 上詣香案前，跪上炷香，又三上香，復位，行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: He went before the incense table, knelt and set incense, then set incense three more times, returned to place, and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the incense table, knelt and set incense, then set incense three more times, returned to position, and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 典儀贊「奠玉帛」，司樂贊「舉樂」，帝詣神位前，跪搢玉帛奠案，復位。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies intoned "Present jade and silk"; the music master intoned "Play the music"; the emperor went before the spirit seat, knelt and placed jade and silk on the table, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies intoned, "Present jade and silk"; the music master intoned, "Play the music"; the emperor went to the spirit seat, knelt and set jade and silk on the table, then returned.

sentences.zh: 典儀贊「進俎」，司樂贊「舉樂」，詣神位前，跪受俎拱舉，復位。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies intoned "Present the offering tray"; the music master intoned "Play the music"; he went before the spirit seat, knelt, received the tray, raised it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies intoned, "Present the offering tray"; the music master intoned, "Play the music"; he went to the spirit seat, knelt, received the tray, raised it in offering, and returned.

sentences.zh: 典儀贊「行初獻禮」，司樂贊「舉初獻樂」，樂作，舞干戚舞，帝詣神位前，跪奠爵，俯伏。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies intoned "Perform the first offering"; the music master intoned "Play the first-offering music"; music sounded and the shield-and-axe dance was performed; the emperor went before the spirit seat, knelt and set the libation cup, and bowed low.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies intoned, "Perform the first offering"; the music master intoned, "Play the first-offering music"; music sounded and the shield-and-axe dance was performed; the emperor went to the spirit seat, knelt and set the libation cup, and bowed low.

sentences.zh: 讀祝官捧祝跪讀訖，行三叩禮。

translations.literal: The prayer reader held the prayer, knelt and read it through, then performed three prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer reader held the prayer, knelt and read it through, then performed three prostrations.

sentences.zh: 自上香至獻爵，配位前儀同。

translations.literal: From setting incense through presenting the libation cup, the rite at collateral seats was the same.
translations.idiomatic: From setting incense through presenting the libation cup, the rite at collateral seats was the same.

sentences.zh: 復位，易文舞。

translations.literal: He returned to position and changed to the civil dance.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to position and changed to the civil dance.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻舞羽籥，儀如初獻，不用祝，分獻官、陪祀官隨行禮。

translations.literal: At the second and final offerings the feather-and-flute dance was performed; the rite was as at the first offering, without the prayer; collateral-offering and attendant officials followed in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the second and final offerings the feather-and-flute dance was performed; the rite matched the first offering but without the prayer; collateral-offering and attendant officials followed in the rite.

sentences.zh: 三獻畢，飲福受胙，帝升壇至飲福位，跪，奉爵官酌福酒，奉胙官奉胙，跪進，受爵、胙，三叩，興，復位。

translations.literal: When the three offerings were complete, he drank the blessing wine and received sacrificial meat; the emperor ascended the altar to the place of drinking the blessing, knelt; the cup-bearer poured the blessing wine and the meat-bearer presented the meat, kneeling to advance them; he received cup and meat, performed three prostrations, rose, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the three offerings were finished, he drank the blessing wine and received sacrificial meat; the emperor ascended to the place of drinking the blessing, knelt; the cup-bearer poured the blessing wine and the meat-bearer presented the meat, kneeling to advance them; he received cup and meat, performed three prostrations, rose, and returned.

sentences.zh: 率群臣行三跪九叩禮，徹饌送神，司樂、典儀贊訖，率群臣行禮如初。

translations.literal: He led the officials in three kneelings and nine prostrations, withdrew the offerings and sent off the spirits; when the music master and master of ceremonies had finished intoning, he led the officials in the rite as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He led the officials in three kneelings and nine prostrations, withdrew the offerings and sent off the spirits; when the music master and master of ceremonies had finished intoning, he led the officials in the rite as before.

sentences.zh: 有司奉祝，次帛，次饌，次香，各詣燎所，唱「望燎」。

translations.literal: The attendants bore the prayer, then silk, then food, then incense, each going to the burning place, intoning "Gaze upon the burning."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants bore the prayer, then silk, then food, then incense, each going to the burning place while intoning, "Gaze upon the burning."

sentences.zh: 帝詣望燎位，半燎，禮成，還大次，解嚴。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the place of gazing upon the burning; when half burned, the rite was complete; he returned to the great tent and the guard was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the place of gazing upon the burning; when half was burned the rite was complete; he returned to the great tent and the guard was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太常官安設神牌，如請神儀。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials reinstalled the spirit tablets as when inviting the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials reinstalled the spirit tablets as when inviting the spirits.

sentences.zh: 若遣代，則行禮三成階下，升降自西階，讀祝跪二成階下。

translations.literal: If a substitute performed, the rite was conducted on the third terrace below; ascent and descent were by the western steps; the prayer was read kneeling on the second terrace below.
translations.idiomatic: If a substitute performed, the rite was conducted on the third terrace below; ascent and descent were by the western steps; the prayer was read kneeling on the second terrace below.

sentences.zh: 罷飲福、受胙禮。

translations.literal: The rites of drinking the blessing and receiving sacrificial meat were omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of drinking the blessing and receiving sacrificial meat were omitted.

sentences.zh: 送燎，退立西偏。

translations.literal: At sending off the burning he withdrew and stood to the west.
translations.idiomatic: At sending off the burning he withdrew and stood to the west.

sentences.zh: 餘如制。

translations.literal: The rest followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed regulation.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，令陪祀官先蒞壇祗候。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, collateral-attending officials were ordered to arrive at the altar first and wait in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, collateral-attending officials were ordered to arrive at the altar first and wait in reverence.

sentences.zh: 方澤，前期但閱祝版。

translations.literal: For the Square Pond, in the preliminary period only the prayer board was inspected.
translations.idiomatic: For the Square Pond, in the preliminary period only the prayer board was inspected.

sentences.zh: 上香畢，奠玉帛，用瘞貍。

translations.literal: After setting incense, jade and silk were presented, using the buried badger.
translations.idiomatic: After setting incense, jade and silk were presented, using the buried badger.

sentences.zh: 餘與郊天同。

translations.literal: The rest was the same as sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The rest matched sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 南郊，詣壇齋宿，自順治十一年著例，無常儀。

translations.literal: For the southern suburb, lodging at the altar for abstention was established as precedent from the eleventh year of Shunzhi, without fixed routine.
translations.idiomatic: For the southern suburb, lodging at the altar for abstention was established as precedent from the eleventh year of Shunzhi, without a fixed routine.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年定制，前一日，鑾儀衛嚴駕陳午門外太和門階下。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong custom was fixed: on the day before, the Imperial Procession Guard arrayed the escort outside the Meridian Gate and below the steps of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong custom was fixed: on the day before, the Imperial Procession Guard arrayed the escort outside the Meridian Gate and below the steps of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 巳刻，太常卿詣乾清門奏請詣齋宮，帝御禮輿出太和門，降輿乘輦，警蹕鳴鐘鼓，至昭亨門外降。

translations.literal: At the si hour the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to report that the emperor should proceed to the abstention palace; the emperor rode the ritual carriage out through the Gate of Supreme Harmony, dismounted and took the imperial carriage; with imperial guard and bells and drums sounding, he reached outside Zhaohang Gate and dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: At the si hour the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to report that the emperor should proceed to the abstention palace; the emperor rode the ritual carriage out through the Gate of Supreme Harmony, dismounted and took the imperial carriage; with imperial guard and bells and drums, he reached outside Zhaohang Gate and dismounted.

sentences.zh: 寺卿導入門左，詣圜丘視壇位。

translations.literal: The director guided him through the left gate and he went to the Round Mound to inspect the altar places.
translations.idiomatic: The director guided him through the left gate to the Round Mound to inspect the altar places.

sentences.zh: 分獻官分詣神庫、神廚視籩豆牲牢。

translations.literal: Collateral-offering officials each went to the spirit storehouse and spirit kitchen to inspect the baskets, beans, and victims.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral-offering officials each went to the spirit storehouse and spirit kitchen to inspect baskets, beans, and victims.

sentences.zh: 帝出內外壝南左門，至神路西升輦，如齋宮。

translations.literal: The emperor went out through the inner and outer south left gates of the precinct, reached the spirit road, and ascended the carriage as at the abstention palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went out through the inner and outer south left gates of the precinct, reached the spirit road, and ascended the carriage as at the abstention palace.

sentences.zh: 從祀官俟帝入，退歸齋所。

translations.literal: Collateral-attending officials waited until the emperor had entered, then withdrew to the abstention lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral-attending officials waited until the emperor had entered, then withdrew to the abstention lodge.

sentences.zh: 翼日屆時，寺卿導入大次，更禮服出，復導駕詣壇行禮，畢，還宮。

translations.literal: On the morrow when the hour came, the director guided him into the great tent; he changed ritual dress and went out; the director again guided the procession to the altar to perform the rite; when finished, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the morrow when the hour came, the director guided him into the great tent; he changed ritual dress and went out; the director again guided the procession to the altar; when the rite was finished he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，高宗六旬，命禮臣酌減升級次數及降輦步行遠近。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the Gaozong Emperor reached sixty, he ordered the ritual officials to reduce the number of terrace ascents and the distance walked after dismounting the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, when the Gaozong Emperor reached sixty, he ordered ritual officials to reduce the number of terrace ascents and the distance walked after dismounting the carriage.

sentences.zh: 議言郊前一日乘步輦如齋宮，自此易禮輿，至神路西降，步詣皇穹宇上香，遣親王視壇。

translations.literal: Deliberation reported: on the day before the suburb ride a palanquin to the abstention palace as before; from there change to the ritual carriage; descend at the spirit road west and walk to the Imperial Vault of Heaven to set incense; send a prince of the blood to inspect the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation reported: on the day before the suburb, ride a palanquin to the abstention palace as before; from there change to the ritual carriage; descend at the west of the spirit road and walk to the Imperial Vault of Heaven to set incense; send a prince of the blood to inspect the altar.

sentences.zh: 祀日自齋宮至神路西階下降輦步入，禮成，即於降輦處乘輿還宮。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, from the abstention palace to the spirit road descend the carriage and walk in; when the rite was complete, take the carriage back to the palace at once from the place of dismounting.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day, from the abstention palace to the spirit road dismount the carriage and walk in; when the rite was complete, return to the palace by carriage immediately from the place of dismounting.

sentences.zh: 行禮時，初升至二成拜位，即升壇上香，復位迎神，升階行奠玉帛禮，以次進俎，三獻暨飲福、受胙，並於此行之。

translations.literal: During the rite, on first ascending to the bowing place on the second terrace he at once ascended the altar to set incense; returning to position to welcome the spirits, he ascended the steps to perform presentation of jade and silk; presenting the offering tray, the three offerings, and drinking the blessing and receiving meat were all performed there.
translations.idiomatic: During the rite, on first ascending to the bowing place on the second terrace he at once ascended the altar to set incense; returning to position to welcome the spirits, he ascended the steps to present jade and silk; presenting the offering tray, the three offerings, and drinking the blessing and receiving meat were all performed there.

sentences.zh: 還拜位，謝福胙，送神，乃卒事。

translations.literal: Returning to the bowing place, he thanked for the blessing meat and sent off the spirits, and only then was the rite concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the bowing place, he thanked for the blessing meat and sent off the spirits, and only then concluded the rite.

sentences.zh: 方澤亦如之。

translations.literal: The Square Pond was treated the same way.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Pond was treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 允行。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 猶慮子孫玩視大典，復於三十九年諭誡，年未六旬，毋減小節，著為令。

translations.literal: Still fearing that posterity might treat the great canon lightly, in the thirty-ninth year he again issued an admonition: those not yet sixty must not reduce small details, and this was made a command.
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing posterity might treat the great canon lightly, in the thirty-ninth year he again issued an admonition: those not yet sixty must not reduce small details, and this was made a command.

sentences.zh: 次年，祀南郊，命諸皇子旁侍觀禮。

translations.literal: The next year, at sacrifice at the southern suburb, he ordered the imperial sons to stand beside him and observe the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, at the southern suburban sacrifice, he ordered the imperial sons to stand beside him and observe the rite.

sentences.zh: 越四年，於是帝年七十矣，諭迎神獻爵暨祖宗配位前上香悉如舊，其獻帛爵諸禮，自本年南郊始，令諸皇子代陳。

translations.literal: Four years later the emperor was seventy; he ordered that welcoming the spirits, presenting the libation cup, and setting incense before the ancestral collateral seats all remain as before, but that from this year's southern suburb onward presentation of silk and libation cups and the like should be performed by the imperial sons as proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later the emperor was seventy; he ordered that welcoming the spirits, presenting the libation cup, and setting incense before the ancestral collateral seats remain as before, but that from this year's southern suburb onward presentation of silk, libation cups, and the like be performed by the imperial sons as proxy.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，帝以春秋高，步履或遜，敕壇上讀祝拜位增設小幄次，然備而未用也。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, as the emperor was advanced in years and his steps sometimes faltered, he ordered small tents added at the prayer-reading and bowing places on the altar, though they were prepared but not used.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year, as the emperor was advanced in years and his steps sometimes faltered, he ordered small tents added at the prayer-reading and bowing places on the altar, though they were prepared but never used.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，祀方澤，配位前獻帛爵，仍皇子代行。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, at sacrifice at the Square Pond, presentation of silk and libation cups before collateral seats was still performed by the imperial sons as proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year, at sacrifice at the Square Pond, presentation of silk and libation cups before collateral seats was still performed by imperial sons as proxy.

sentences.zh: 歷仁宗朝，郊祀各儀節，悉遵高宗舊制雲。

translations.literal: Through the Renzong reign, each ritual detail of suburban sacrifice followed the Gaozong Emperor's former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Renzong reign, each ritual detail of suburban sacrifice followed the Gaozong Emperor's former regulations.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，林清變起，計日敉平，會長至祀圜丘，諭先一日赴壇不升輦，自宮至皇穹宇入齋宮，並御肩輿，用答嘉貺。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, when the Lin Qing disturbance arose, it was pacified within the expected days; at the winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound, an edict ordered that on the day before he go to the altar without ascending the carriage, from the palace to the Imperial Vault of Heaven and into the abstention palace, all by shoulder-borne sedan, in thanks for the gracious blessing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, when the Lin Qing disturbance arose, it was pacified within the expected days; at the winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound, an edict ordered that on the day before he go to the altar without riding the carriage, from the palace to the Imperial Vault of Heaven and into the abstention palace—all by shoulder sedan—in thanks for the gracious blessing.

sentences.zh: 宣統嗣位，監國攝行郊祀，祀日詣壇，不齋宿，百官不迎送。

translations.literal: When Xuantong succeeded, the regent performed the suburban sacrifice by proxy; on the sacrifice day he went to the altar without lodging for abstention, and officials did not welcome or escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuantong succeeded, the regent performed suburban sacrifice by proxy; on the sacrifice day he went to the altar without lodging for abstention, and officials did not welcome or escort.

sentences.zh: 出入升降，仍由右門，在右階行禮。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving, ascending and descending, still used the right gate and performed the rite on the right steps.
translations.idiomatic: Entering and leaving, ascending and descending, still used the right gate and performed the rite on the right steps.

sentences.zh: 拜位設第二成，視帝位少後。

translations.literal: The bowing place was set on the second terrace, slightly behind the emperor's place.
translations.idiomatic: The bowing place was set on the second terrace, slightly behind the emperor's place.

sentences.zh: 去黃幄。

translations.literal: The yellow tent was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow tent was removed.

sentences.zh: 即於行禮處受胙，畢，進福酒、胙肉。

translations.literal: He received sacrificial meat at once at the place of performing the rite; when finished, blessing wine and sacrificial meat were advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He received sacrificial meat at once at the place of performing the rite; when finished, blessing wine and sacrificial meat were advanced.

sentences.zh: 餘同親祀儀。

translations.literal: The rest follows the rites for personal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The rest follows the rites for sacrifice performed in person.

sentences.zh: 郊祀配饗順治五年冬至，祀圜丘，奉太祖配。

translations.literal: Collateral offerings at suburban sacrifice: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, at the winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound, Taizu was offered as collateral.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral offerings at suburban sacrifice: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, at the winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound, Taizu was offered as collateral spirit.

sentences.zh: 十四年諭曰：「太祖肇興帝業，太宗繼述皇猷，功德並隆，咸宜崇祀。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict stated: "Taizu founded the imperial enterprise and Taizong continued the royal design; their merit and virtue alike were lofty, and both should be honored in sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict stated, "Taizu founded the imperial enterprise and Taizong continued the royal design; their merit and virtue were equally great, and both should be honored in sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 以後大祀天地，益奉太宗配饗。

translations.literal: Henceforth at great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Taizong was also offered as collateral.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Taizong was also added as collateral offering.

sentences.zh: 於是上辛祈穀，上帝位東奉太祖神位，卜吉奉太宗位於其西。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the first shang day of the prayer for grain, the seat of the Supreme Lord was in the east with the spirit tablet of Taizu, and on an auspicious day the tablet of Taizong was placed to its west.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon at the first shang day of the prayer for grain, the Supreme Lord's seat was in the east with the spirit tablet of Taizu; on an auspicious day the tablet of Taizong was placed to its west.

sentences.zh: 夏至配方澤如初禮。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice, collateral offering at the Square Pond followed the original rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice, collateral offering at the Square Pond followed the original rite.

sentences.zh: 十七年，行大饗殿合祀禮，尋罷。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the rite of combined sacrifice at the Grand Offeringing Hall was performed, but was soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the rite of combined sacrifice at the Grand Offeringing Hall was performed, but was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年冬至，祀南郊，用禮臣言，奉世祖配饗上帝，越九日，配饗皇地祇，詣方澤行禮。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of the sixth year of Kangxi, at sacrifice at the southern suburb, following the ritual officials' proposal, Shizu was offered as collateral to the Supreme Lord; nine days later he was offered as collateral to Imperial Earth at the Square Pond, where the emperor went to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of the sixth year of Kangxi, at sacrifice at the southern suburb, following the ritual officials' proposal, Shizu was offered as collateral to the Supreme Lord; nine days later he was offered as collateral to Imperial Earth at the Square Pond, where the emperor went to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 九年，祈穀亦如之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the prayer for grain was treated the same way.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the prayer for grain was treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，奉聖祖配大饗殿，次太宗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, the Sage Ancestor was offered at the Grand Offeringing Hall, below Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng, the Sage Ancestor was offered at the Grand Offeringing Hall, below Taizong.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，高宗嗣服，諭言：「皇考世宗，德侔造化，宜祀郊壇。」

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year, when the Gaozong Emperor succeeded to mourning dress, he stated: "My imperial father the Shizong Emperor, whose virtue matches creation and transformation, should be sacrificed at the suburban altars."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year, when the Gaozong Emperor succeeded to mourning dress, he stated, "My imperial father the Shizong Emperor, whose virtue matches creation and transformation, should be sacrificed at the suburban altars."

sentences.zh: 命議禮以聞。

translations.literal: He ordered ritual deliberation to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered ritual deliberation to be reported.

sentences.zh: 議者謂宜乾隆二年冬至配圜丘，三年孟春上辛配大饗殿，夏至配方澤。

translations.literal: Deliberators held that he should be offered at the Round Mound at the winter solstice of the second year of Qianlong, at the Grand Offeringing Hall on the first shang day of the first month of the third year, and at the Square Pond at the summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators held that he should be offered at the Round Mound at the winter solstice of the second year of Qianlong, at the Grand Offeringing Hall on the first shang day of the first month of the third year, and at the Square Pond at the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 帝意以為祔廟後配饗，去夏至近、冬至遠。

translations.literal: The emperor thought that after enshrinement in the ancestral temple, collateral offering should follow; the summer solstice was near and the winter solstice far.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought that after enshrinement in the ancestral temple, collateral offering should follow; the summer solstice was near and the winter solstice far.

sentences.zh: 先配方澤，前後已歧。

translations.literal: To offer at the Square Pond first would already create a discrepancy in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: To offer at the Square Pond first would already create a discrepancy in sequence.

sentences.zh: 若俟南郊，時日又曠。

translations.literal: If one waited for the southern suburb, the time would again be too long delayed.
translations.idiomatic: If one waited for the southern suburb, the time would again be too long delayed.

sentences.zh: 考之舊典，世祖、太宗配饗天地，莫不先圜丘後方澤，時或翼日、或旬日，禮儀粲然。

translations.literal: Examining the former canon, when Shizu and Taizong were offered as collateral to Heaven and Earth, it was always first the Round Mound and then the Square Pond, sometimes on the morrow, sometimes within ten days—the ritual was clearly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the former canon, when Shizu and Taizong were offered as collateral to Heaven and Earth, it was always first the Round Mound and then the Square Pond, sometimes on the morrow, sometimes within ten days—the ritual was clearly ordered.

sentences.zh: 稽之經傳，成周郊祀后稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂，即月令所謂「季秋，大饗帝」也。

translations.literal: Examining the classics and commentaries, in the Zhou suburban sacrifice Hou Ji was offered to match Heaven, and King Wen was honored in the Bright Hall—that is what the Monthly Ordinances calls "in the last month of autumn, the great feast to the Lord."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the classics and commentaries, in the Zhou suburban sacrifice Hou Ji was offered to match Heaven, and King Wen was honored in the Bright Hall—that is what the Monthly Ordinances calls "in the last month of autumn, the great feast to the Lord."

sentences.zh: 召誥「三日丁巳用牲於郊」。

translations.literal: The Announcement of Duke Shao says, "On the third day, the day dingsi, victims were used at the suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The Announcement of Duke Shao says, "On the third day, the day dingsi, victims were used at the suburb."

sentences.zh: 釋者謂非常祀而祭天，以告即位也。

translations.literal: Commentators hold this was not the regular sacrifice but sacrifice to Heaven to announce assumption of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators hold this was not the regular sacrifice but sacrifice to Heaven to announce assumption of the throne.

sentences.zh: 宋皇祐三年，以大慶殿為明堂，合祭天地，三聖並侑，古者因事而郊，不必定在二至。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou of Song, the Great Celebration Hall was made the Bright Hall for combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with the three sage emperors all as collateral—ancients sacrificed at the suburb according to the occasion, not necessarily fixed at the two solstices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangyou of Song, the Great Celebration Hall was made the Bright Hall for combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with the three sage emperors all as collateral—ancients sacrificed at the suburb according to the occasion, not necessarily fixed at the two solstices.

sentences.zh: 因諭來年世宗配天大禮，准此行事。

translations.literal: Therefore he ordered that next year's great rite of the Shizong Emperor as collateral to Heaven should proceed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he ordered that next year's great rite of the Shizong Emperor as collateral to Heaven should proceed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，遂諏吉夏至前奉世宗配圜丘。

translations.literal: The following year, an auspicious day was chosen before the summer solstice to offer the Shizong Emperor at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, an auspicious day was chosen before the summer solstice to offer the Shizong Emperor at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 餘如議。

translations.literal: The rest followed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 先是部臣進升配儀，未議及祗見上帝。

translations.literal: Earlier the ministry had submitted the rites for elevation to collateral offering but had not deliberated paying respects to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the ministry had submitted the rites for elevation to collateral offering but had not deliberated paying respects to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「皇考祔廟，先見祖宗，然後升座，今行配饗，先見上帝，於義始允。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When my imperial father was enshrined in the temple, he first paid respects to the ancestors and only then took his seat; now in performing collateral offering, he should first pay respects to the Supreme Lord—only then is the meaning proper."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When my imperial father was enshrined in the temple, he first paid respects to the ancestors and only then took his seat; now in performing collateral offering, he should first pay respects to the Supreme Lord—only then is the meaning proper."

sentences.zh: 已，所司具儀上。

translations.literal: When finished, the responsible office submitted the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the responsible office submitted the rites.

sentences.zh: 於是祀南郊奉世宗神位祗見上帝，夏至祀方澤，祗見皇地祇，位並次世祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon at sacrifice at the southern suburb the Shizong Emperor's spirit tablet paid respects to the Supreme Lord; at the summer solstice sacrifice at the Square Pond he paid respects to Imperial Earth, his place both below Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon at sacrifice at the southern suburb the Shizong Emperor's spirit tablet paid respects to the Supreme Lord; at the summer solstice sacrifice at the Square Pond he paid respects to Imperial Earth, his place both below Shizu.

sentences.zh: 嗣是升配皆先祗見，以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter every elevation to collateral offering first paid respects, and this became constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every elevation to collateral offering first paid respects, and this became constant practice.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，奉高宗配饗，道光元年，奉仁宗配饗，並如儀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing the Gaozong Emperor was offered as collateral; in the first year of Daoguang the Renzong Emperor was offered—all according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing the Gaozong Emperor was offered as collateral; in the first year of Daoguang the Renzong Emperor was offered—all according to rite.

sentences.zh: 三十年，帝弗豫，遺命罷郊配，略謂：「禘郊祖宗，伊古所重，我朝首太祖訖仁宗。

sentences.zh: 步詣皇乾殿上香，畢，還齋宮，親王視壇位。

translations.literal: He walked to the Hall of Imperial Heaven to set incense; when finished he returned to the abstention palace, and a prince of the blood inspected the altar places.
translations.idiomatic: He walked to the Hall of Imperial Heaven to set incense; when finished he returned to the abstention palace, and a prince of the blood inspected the altar places.

sentences.zh: 祀日出齋宮，乘輦，至甬道正中，易禮輿，至神路西降。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day he left the abstention palace by carriage; reaching the middle of the spirit terrace he changed to the ritual carriage; at the spirit road west he dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day he left the abstention palace by carriage; reaching the middle of the spirit terrace he changed to the ritual carriage; at the spirit road west he dismounted.

sentences.zh: 自磚城步就幄次，入左門，禮同圜丘。

translations.literal: From the brick city he walked to the tent, entered the left gate; the rite was the same as at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: From the brick city he walked to the tent, entered the left gate; the rite was the same as at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 四十七年正月四日上辛，禮臣先期請改次辛便，帝曰：「上辛在正月三日前，為須隔年齋戒也；

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, on the fourth day of the first month—the first shang day—ritual officials beforehand asked to change to the next shang day for convenience. The Emperor said: "If the first shang day falls before the third day of the first month, it is because year-spanning abstention is required;
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year the first shang day fell on the fourth day of the first month. Ritual officials had asked in advance to switch to the next shang day for convenience. The Emperor replied, "When the first shang day comes before the third day of the first month, that is because abstention must span the old and new year;

sentences.zh: 在四日前，為因聖母祝釐也。

translations.literal: if it falls before the fourth day, it is because of birthday congratulations for the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: when it falls before the fourth day, that is on account of the Empress Dowager's birthday congratulations.

sentences.zh: 茲非昔比，奚改為？

translations.literal: Now things are not as they once were—why change it?
translations.idiomatic: Times are not what they were—why alter it?

sentences.zh: 其仍用上辛，著為例。」

translations.literal: Let the first shang day still be used, and establish this as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Continue to use the first shang day, and make this the standing rule."

sentences.zh: 又諭：「孟春祈穀，所以迓陽氣，兆農祥。

translations.literal: He also instructed: "The prayer for grain in early spring is to welcome the yang force and augur agricultural blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared: "The early-spring prayer for grain welcomes the yang qi and foretells a good harvest.

sentences.zh: 考諸經傳，是立春後上辛，非元旦後上辛也。

translations.literal: Examining the classics and commentaries, it should be the first shang day after the Establishment of Spring, not the first shang day after New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: A review of the classics shows that the proper date is the first shang day after the Establishment of Spring—not the first shang day after New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 惟在月初，舊臘，即當齋戒。

translations.literal: Only because it falls at the month's beginning—in the old twelfth month—must one abstain.
translations.idiomatic: It falls only at the month's opening, during the old twelfth month, and so abstention must begin then.

sentences.zh: 然太廟祫祭，大禮攸關，宮中拜神，國俗所在。

translations.literal: Yet the Grand Ancestral Temple's autumnal joint sacrifice is a great rite of moment; worship of the spirits within the palace is entrenched in national custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Grand Ancestral Temple's autumnal joint sacrifice is a major state ceremony, and worship within the palace is a fixed national custom.

sentences.zh: 若以齋期行此，似非專一致敬之道。」

translations.literal: If these are performed during the abstention period, it seems not the way of single-minded reverence."
translations.idiomatic: To carry out these observances during the abstention period would hardly be the path of wholehearted devotion."

sentences.zh: 因下廷臣議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he referred the matter to court officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted the question to the court for discussion.

sentences.zh: 尋奏：「上辛以立春後所得為準，與其用十二月上辛，不如用正月上辛，以重歲首。

translations.literal: Soon they reported: "The first shang day should be determined by what falls after the Establishment of Spring; rather than using the first shang day of the twelfth month, it is better to use the first shang day of the first month, to honor the year's opening.
translations.idiomatic: They soon memorialized: "The first shang day should be reckoned from what comes after the Establishment of Spring. Better to use the first shang day of the first month than the first shang day of the twelfth, so as to give weight to the year's beginning.

sentences.zh: 如值三日前，則改次辛。

translations.literal: If it falls before the third day, then change to the next shang day.
translations.idiomatic: If it falls before the third day, switch to the next shang day.

sentences.zh: 或四日前，則應一日齋戒，是日未入齋宮，宮殿拜祭，各不相妨。

translations.literal: If before the fourth day, then observe one day's abstention; on that day one has not yet entered the Abstention Palace—palace worship and sacrifice need not interfere with each other.
translations.idiomatic: If it falls before the fourth day, observe a single day of abstention; on that day one has not yet entered the Abstention Palace, so palace worship and sacrifice may proceed without conflict.

sentences.zh: 毋庸改期。」

translations.literal: There is no need to change the date."
translations.idiomatic: The date need not be changed."

sentences.zh: 允行。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，祈穀，帝患宿疾，敕禮臣酌損儀文。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, at the prayer for grain, the Emperor suffered from a chronic ailment and ordered ritual officials to reduce the ritual text as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, during the prayer for grain, the Emperor was troubled by a long-standing illness and directed ritual officials to trim the ceremonial protocol as needed.

sentences.zh: 侍郎宋晉請仍舊貫遣代行。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Song Jin asked to follow old practice and send a substitute.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Song Jin requested that old practice be kept and a proxy be sent in his stead.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是非輕改舊章也，應天以實不以文，此意宜共喻之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is not lightly altering old regulations—it is responding to Heaven with substance rather than with form; this meaning should be understood by all."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "This is no casual change to established rites. One answers Heaven with sincerity, not with mere ceremony—and everyone should grasp that intent."

sentences.zh: 雩祀關外未嘗行。

translations.literal: The rain sacrifice had never been performed outside the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Rain sacrifices had never been conducted beyond the Pass.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年夏旱，世祖始禱雨圜丘，前期齋三日，冠服淺色，禁屠宰，罷刑名。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi there was summer drought; the Shizu Emperor first prayed for rain at the Round Mound—three days' abstention beforehand, light-colored caps and robes, prohibition of slaughter, suspension of criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, during a summer drought, the Shizu Emperor first prayed for rain at the Round Mound. For three days beforehand he abstained, wore light-colored dress, forbade slaughter, and suspended criminal proceedings.

sentences.zh: 屆期，帝素服步入壇，不除道，不陳鹵簿，壇上設酒果、香鐙、祝帛暨熟牛脯醢，祭時不奏樂，不設配位，不奠玉，不飲福、受胙。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, the Emperor in plain robes walked into the altar, without clearing the road or displaying the guard of honor; on the altar were set wine and fruit, incense lamps, prayer silks, and cooked beef with condiments; at sacrifice no music was played, no collateral seats were set, no jade was offered, and no drinking of blessing wine or receiving of sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the Emperor entered the altar in plain robes on foot, without clearing the road or parading the guard of honor. The altar held wine and fruit, incense lamps, prayer silks, and cooked beef with sauces. During the rite there was no music, no collateral seats, no jade offering, and no blessing wine or sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 餘如冬至祀儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the winter solstice sacrificial protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed winter solstice sacrifice protocol.

sentences.zh: 其方澤、社稷、神祇諸壇，則遣官蒞祭。

translations.literal: As for the Square Pond, soil and grain, and spirits altars, officials were dispatched to preside at sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At the Square Pond, the altars of soil and grain, and the altars of the spirits, officials were sent to conduct the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 既得雨，越三日，遣官報祀。

translations.literal: Once rain had fallen, after three days officials were dispatched to report the sacrifice of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: After rain came, officials were sent three days later to perform the thank-offering report sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 定躬禱郊壇儀自此始。

translations.literal: The fixing of ritual for the Emperor's personal prayer at the suburban altars began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The established protocol for the Emperor's personal prayer at the suburban altars dates from this time.

sentences.zh: 越三年又旱，卜吉致齋，步至南郊，躬親告祭。

translations.literal: Three years later drought came again; an auspicious day was divined and abstention observed; he walked to the southern suburb and personally performed the announcement sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later drought returned. An auspicious day was chosen, abstention was observed, and he walked to the southern suburb to offer the announcement sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 於時天無片雲，頃之乃大雨。

translations.literal: At that time there was not a cloud in the sky; shortly afterward great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: The sky was utterly cloudless; moments later a heavy rain poured down.

sentences.zh: 報祀如初。

translations.literal: The thank-offering sacrifice was as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The thank-offering was conducted as before.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年夏旱，詔百官修省，禮部祈雨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi there was summer drought; an edict ordered all officials to examine themselves, and the Board of Rites prayed for rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kangxi a summer drought struck. An edict called on all officials to practice self-examination, and the Board of Rites performed rain prayers.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝親禱。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor prayed in person.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Emperor prayed in person.

sentences.zh: 自後躬祀以為常。

translations.literal: After this personal sacrifice became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter personal sacrifice became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，親制祝文祈告，雨立降。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he personally composed the prayer text and made entreaty—and rain fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he wrote the prayer text himself and offered his petition; rain fell immediately.

sentences.zh: 又嘗設壇宮禁，跽禱三晝夜，日惟淡食，越四日，步禱天壇，雨驟澍，步還宮，衣履霑濕雲。

translations.literal: He also once set up an altar within the Forbidden City, knelt in prayer for three days and nights, eating only plain food by day; after four days he walked to pray at the Heaven Altar; rain suddenly poured; walking back to the palace, his clothes and shoes were soaked through.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he erected an altar inside the Forbidden City and knelt in prayer for three days and nights, taking only plain food each day. Four days later he walked to the Heaven Altar to pray; rain burst forth at once. He walked back to the palace with his clothes and shoes drenched.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，御史徐以升奏言：「春秋傳：『龍見而雩，為百穀祈膏雨也。』

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong, Censor Xu Yisheng memorialized: "The Spring and Autumn Annals commentary: 'When the dragon appears, perform the rain sacrifice—to pray for rich rain for the hundred grains.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong, Censor Xu Yisheng submitted a memorial citing the Spring and Autumn commentary: "When the dragon appears, perform the rain sacrifice, to seek nourishing rain for the hundred grains.

sentences.zh: 祭法：『雩宗，祭水旱也。』

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrificial Rites: 'The Rain-Altar Lord—sacrifices for flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrificial Rites states: "The Rain-Altar Lord is worshipped against flood and drought."

sentences.zh: 禮月令：『雩，帝用盛樂，命百縣雩祀，祀百辟卿士有益於民者，以祈穀實，是為常雩。』

translations.literal: The ritual Monthly Ordinances: 'For the rain sacrifice, the Emperor uses splendid music and orders the hundred districts to perform rain sacrifice, sacrificing to the hundred noble ministers and officers who benefit the people, to pray for full grain—this is the regular rain sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual Monthly Ordinances says: "For the rain sacrifice the Emperor employs grand music and commands the hundred districts to perform rain rites, offering to the hundred lords and officers who serve the people, praying for a full harvest—this is the regular rain sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 周禮：『稻人，旱又共雩斂。』

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: 'The rice officer—in drought again provides jointly for rain sacrifice and levies.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou records: "The rice officer, in time of drought, again supplies materials jointly for rain sacrifice and collection."

sentences.zh: 春秋書雩二十有一，有一月再雩者，旱甚也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records twenty-one rain sacrifices; there are cases of two rain sacrifices in one month—drought was severe.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records twenty-one rain sacrifices, including instances of two in a single month—signs of severe drought.

sentences.zh: 是又因旱而雩。

translations.literal: This, then, is performing rain sacrifice again because of drought.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rain sacrifice was also performed when drought struck.

sentences.zh: 考雩義為吁嗟求雨，其制，為壇南郊旁，故魯南門為雩門，西漢始廢，旱輒禱郊廟。

translations.literal: Examining the meaning of rain sacrifice, it is to sigh and seek rain; its institution was to set up an altar beside the southern suburb—hence Lu's southern gate was called the Rain Gate; the Western Han first abolished it, and in drought one prayed at the suburban altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: The rain sacrifice means to cry out and beg for rain. By ancient institution an altar stood beside the southern suburb—hence Lu's southern gate was named the Rain Gate. The Western Han first abolished the practice; thereafter drought prompted prayer at suburban altars and temples.

sentences.zh: 晉永和立壇南郊，梁武帝始徙東，改燔燎從坎瘞。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era of Jin an altar was established at the southern suburb; Emperor Wu of Liang first moved it east and changed from burning offerings to burying them in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin's Yonghe reign an altar was erected at the southern suburb. Emperor Wu of Liang first relocated it eastward and replaced burnt offerings with burial in a pit.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗復舊制。

translations.literal: Tang Taizong restored the old institution.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Taizong restored the former practice.

sentences.zh: 宋時孟夏雩祀上帝。

translations.literal: In Song times, in early summer rain sacrifice was offered to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song, the early-summer rain sacrifice was offered to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 明建壇泰元門東，制一成，旱則禱。

translations.literal: In Ming an altar was built east of the Gate of Grand Primality, with one tier; in drought one prayed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming built an altar east of the Gate of Grand Primality, with a single terrace; in drought one prayed there.

sentences.zh: 我朝雩祭無壇，典制似闕，應度地建立，以符古義。」

translations.literal: Our dynasty's rain sacrifice has no altar—the canonical institution seems lacking; ground should be surveyed and an altar established to accord with ancient meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's rain rites have no dedicated altar—a gap in canonical practice. Ground should be chosen and an altar built to restore ancient meaning."

sentences.zh: 下禮臣議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to ritual officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to ritual officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 議言：「孟夏龍見，擇日行常雩，祀圜丘，奉列祖配。

translations.literal: They deliberated: "When the dragon appears in early summer, choose a day to perform the regular rain sacrifice, sacrificing at the Round Mound with the successive ancestors as collateral spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Their recommendation read: "When the dragon appears in early summer, select a day for the regular rain sacrifice at the Round Mound, with the successive ancestors as collateral spirits.

sentences.zh: 四從壇，皆如禮。

translations.literal: The four secondary altars—all according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The four secondary altars should all follow established ritual.

sentences.zh: 孟夏後旱，則仿唐制，祭神祇、社稷、宗廟。

translations.literal: After early summer, if drought occurs, then following the Tang institution, sacrifice at the altars of spirits, soil and grain, and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: If drought persists after early summer, follow the Tang precedent: sacrifice at the altars of the spirits, soil and grain, and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 七日一祈，不足，仍分禱。

translations.literal: Once every seven days pray; if insufficient, still divide prayer among altars.
translations.idiomatic: Pray once every seven days; if that proves inadequate, continue divided prayer at separate altars.

sentences.zh: 旱甚，大雩。

translations.literal: If drought is severe, the Great Rain Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In extreme drought, perform the Great Rain Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 令甲，祈雨必望祭四海，至是罷之。

translations.literal: By standing decree, praying for rain had required worship of the Four Seas on the full-moon day—at this time that was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under prior regulation, rain prayer had required full-moon worship of the Four Seas; this requirement was now abolished.

sentences.zh: 又行大雩，用舞童十六人，衣玄衣，分八列，執羽翳，三獻，樂止，乃按舞。

translations.literal: When performing the Great Rain Sacrifice again, use sixteen dancing youths, dressed in dark robes, in eight columns, holding feather fans; after three presentations, when music stops, then perform the dance.
translations.idiomatic: For the Great Rain Sacrifice, sixteen dancing youths in dark robes stand in eight ranks, holding feather fans. After three presentations the music ceases and the dance begins.

sentences.zh: 歌御制雲漢詩八章，畢，望燎。

translations.literal: Sing the Emperor's eight stanzas of the Clouds Broad poem; when finished, gaze at the burning of offerings.
translations.idiomatic: They sing the Emperor's eight stanzas of the Broad Clouds ode; when done, they perform the gazing-at-burning rite.

sentences.zh: 餘同常雩。

translations.literal: The remainder follows the regular rain sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: All else follows the regular rain sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 至久雨祈晴，宜仿春秋傳鼓用牲，通考禜祭制，伐鼓祀少牢。

translations.literal: For prolonged rain and prayer for clear weather, one should follow the Spring and Autumn Annals commentary on beating drums and using victims, and the Comprehensive Examination's rain-clearing sacrifice institution—beat drums and sacrifice a minor victim.
translations.idiomatic: When long rain calls for prayer for clear skies, follow the Spring and Autumn commentary on drum-beating with victims and the Comprehensive Examination's rain-clearing rite: beat drums and offer a minor victim.

sentences.zh: 禜祭國門，雨不止，則伐鼓用牲於社。

translations.literal: Perform the rain-clearing sacrifice at the state gate; if rain does not stop, then beat drums and use victims at the soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct the rain-clearing sacrifice at the state gate; if rain still will not cease, beat drums and offer victims at the soil altar.

sentences.zh: 罷分禱，停僧道官建壇諷經。

translations.literal: Abolish divided prayer; stop Buddhist and Daoist officials from building altars and intoning scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Divided prayer was abolished, and Buddhist and Daoist officials were forbidden to erect altars and chant scriptures.

sentences.zh: 其直省州、縣舊置耤田壇祀，仍依雍正四年例。

translations.literal: As for the provinces, prefectures, and counties with their old established plow-field altars for sacrifice, follow still the fourth year of Yongzheng precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces, prefectures, and counties that maintained plow-field altars for sacrifice should continue under the fourth-year Yongzheng precedent.

sentences.zh: 孟夏行常雩，患旱，先祭境內山川，次社稷。

translations.literal: In early summer perform the regular rain sacrifice; if drought afflicts, first sacrifice to mountains and rivers within the jurisdiction, then to soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In early summer perform the regular rain sacrifice. When drought strikes, sacrifice first to local mountains and rivers, then to soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 患霪潦祈晴，如京師式。」

translations.literal: If afflicted by prolonged floods and praying for clear weather, follow the capital model."
translations.idiomatic: When excessive rain demands prayer for clear skies, follow the capital's procedure."

sentences.zh: 十七年，增祈雨報祭樂章。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, hymn texts for rain-prayer thank-offering sacrifice were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, musical hymn texts were added for rain-prayer thank-offering sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，常雩不雨，帝步禱社稷壇，仍用玉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the regular rain sacrifice brought no rain; the Emperor walked to pray at the soil and grain altar, still using jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the regular rain sacrifice failed to bring rain. The Emperor walked to the soil and grain altar to pray, still presenting jade.

sentences.zh: 六月大雩，親制祝文，定儀節。

translations.literal: In the sixth month came the Great Rain Sacrifice; he personally composed the prayer text and fixed the ritual program.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he performed the Great Rain Sacrifice, composing the prayer text himself and setting the ceremonial order.

sentences.zh: 前一日，帝常服視祝版，詣壇齋宿，去鹵簿，停樂。

translations.literal: On the day before, in regular dress the Emperor inspected the prayer board, proceeded to the altar for abstention overnight, dispensed with the guard of honor, and stopped music.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rite the Emperor, in regular dress, inspected the prayer board, lodged overnight at the altar in abstention, set aside the guard of honor, and halted music.

sentences.zh: 出宮用騎，扈駕大臣常服導從。

translations.literal: Leaving the palace he rode; accompanying ministers in regular dress guided and followed.
translations.idiomatic: He left the palace on horseback, with accompanying ministers in regular dress leading and following the procession.

sentences.zh: 至南郊，步入壇，視位上香。

translations.literal: Reaching the southern suburb, he walked into the altar, inspected the seats, and burned incense.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburb he entered the altar on foot, inspected the ritual seats, and offered incense.

sentences.zh: 祀日，帝雨冠素服步禱，從臣亦如之。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, the Emperor wore a rain cap and plain robes and walked in prayer; attendant ministers did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice the Emperor wore a rain cap and plain robes and walked in prayer, and the attending ministers did the same.

sentences.zh: 不燔柴，不晉俎，不飲福、受胙。

translations.literal: No burning of firewood, no advancing of sacrificial trays, no drinking of blessing wine or receiving of sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: There was no firewood burning, no advancing of sacrificial trays, and no blessing wine or sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 三獻畢，舞童舞羽、歌詩，退，皆如儀。

translations.literal: After three presentations were complete, the dancing youths danced with feathers and sang the poems; withdrawal—all according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the three presentations were finished, the dancing youths performed the feather dance and sang the hymns; the withdrawal followed standard protocol.

sentences.zh: 帝率★臣三拜，徹饌，望燎。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the ministers in three prostrations, removed the offerings, and gazed at the burning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the ministers in three bows, cleared the offerings, and performed the gazing-at-burning rite.

sentences.zh: 禮成，還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony concluded and he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，帝以年老，命酌損儀節視圜丘。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, the Emperor being advanced in age, ordered that ritual procedures be appropriately reduced, taking the Round Mound rite as reference.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, citing his advanced age, the Emperor ordered that ceremonial steps be trimmed as appropriate, using the Round Mound sacrifice as the model.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，以欽天監雩祀擇日，頻年恆在立夏節，殊乖古義，敕立夏後數日蠲吉行。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, because the Qintianjian's chosen dates for rain sacrifice in successive years had always fallen on the Beginning of Summer festival—greatly at odds with ancient meaning—an edict ordered that after Beginning of Summer several days an auspicious day be chosen for performance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, because the Qintianjian had repeatedly scheduled rain sacrifices on the Beginning of Summer—a clear departure from ancient practice—an edict required that an auspicious day be chosen several days after Beginning of Summer.

sentences.zh: 著為例。

translations.literal: This was established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This became the standing rule.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年六月大雩，親制祝文，省躬思過。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang, in the sixth month came the Great Rain Sacrifice; he personally composed the prayer text and examined himself, reflecting on faults.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daoguang, during the sixth-month Great Rain Sacrifice, he wrote the prayer text himself and searched his own conduct for failings.

sentences.zh: 是夕雨。

translations.literal: That evening rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Rain came that same evening.

sentences.zh: 報謝如常儀。

translations.literal: The thank-offering was according to usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The thank-offering followed the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 御史陳焯請再申虔禱。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Chao asked to perform devout prayer again.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Chao requested another round of earnest prayer.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「祭法有祈有報。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Record of Sacrificial Rites distinguishes between prayer and thank-offering.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "The Record of Sacrificial Rites draws a line between prayer and thank-offering.

sentences.zh: 以報為祈，非禮也。

translations.literal: To take thank-offering as prayer is not ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: To treat a thank-offering as prayer is improper.

sentences.zh: 其勿逾舊制。」

translations.literal: Do not exceed the old institution."
translations.idiomatic: Do not go beyond the old institution."

sentences.zh: 天神順治初，定雲、雨、風、雷。

translations.literal: Heaven Spirits: at the beginning of Shunzhi, cloud, rain, wind, and thunder were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Spirits: at the start of the Shunzhi reign, cloud, rain, wind, and thunder were established.

sentences.zh: 既配饗圜丘，並建天神壇位先農壇南，專祀之。
