translations.literal: Having already been collateral spirits at the Round Mound feast, an altar to the Heaven Spirits was also established south of the First Farmer Altar for their exclusive worship.
translations.idiomatic: Already serving as collateral spirits at the Round Mound feast, they were also given a dedicated Heaven Spirits altar south of the First Farmer Altar for exclusive worship.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，諭建風神廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, an edict ordered the building of a Wind Spirit Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng an edict directed the construction of a Wind Spirit Temple.

sentences.zh: 禮臣言：「周禮燎祀飌師，鄭康成注風師為箕星，即虞書六宗之一。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "The Rites of Zhou burns offerings to the Wind Master; Zheng Xuan annotated that the Wind Master is the Sieve Star—that is, one of the Six Honored Ones in the Book of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials reported: "The Rites of Zhou prescribes burnt offerings to the Wind Master. Zheng Xuan identified the Wind Master with the Sieve Star—one of the Six Honored Ones in the Book of Yu.

sentences.zh: 馬端臨謂，周制立春丑日，祭風師國城東北，蓋東北箕星之次，丑亦應箕位。

translations.literal: Ma Duanlin states: under Zhou institution, on the ox day after Establishment of Spring, the Wind Master was sacrificed to at the northeast of the capital city—presumably the seat of the northeast Sieve Star; the ox day also corresponds to the Sieve's position.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Duanlin notes that under Zhou practice the Wind Master was sacrificed on the ox day after the Establishment of Spring at the northeast corner of the capital—the quarter of the northeast Sieve Star, with the ox day matching the Sieve's astrological position.

sentences.zh: 漢劉歆等議立風伯廟於東郊。

translations.literal: In Han, Liu Xin and others deliberated establishing a Wind Lord Temple at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: During the Han, Liu Xin and others proposed building a Wind Lord Temple at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 東漢縣邑，常以丙戌日祀之戌地。

translations.literal: In Eastern Han, counties and districts commonly sacrificed on the bing-xu day at the xu quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Han, counties and districts commonly worshipped on the bing-xu day in the xu quarter.

sentences.zh: 唐制就箕星位為壇，宋仍之。

translations.literal: Under Tang institution an altar was placed at the Sieve Star's position; Song continued this.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang placed an altar at the Sieve Star's position, and the Song kept the practice.

sentences.zh: 今卜地景山東，適當箕位，建廟為宜。

translations.literal: Now, having divined ground east of Jingshan—fitting exactly the Sieve Star's position—to build a temple there is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Ground east of Jingshan has now been chosen by divination, falling precisely in the Sieve Star's quarter; a temple should be built there.

sentences.zh: 歲以立春後丑日祭。」

translations.literal: Each year sacrifice on the ox day after Establishment of Spring."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice each year on the ox day after the Establishment of Spring."

sentences.zh: 允行。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 規制仿時應宮，錫號「應時顯佑」，廟曰宣仁。

translations.literal: The design copied the Seasonal Responsiveness Palace; the bestowed title was "Manifest Aid in Season," and the temple was called Broad Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Its layout followed the Seasonal Responsiveness Palace. The conferred title was "Manifest Aid in Season," and the temple was named Broad Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 前殿祀風伯，後殿祀八風神。

translations.literal: The front hall worships the Wind Lord; the rear hall worships the Eight Wind Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The front hall enshrines the Wind Lord; the rear hall enshrines the Eight Wind Spirits.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以雲師、雷師尚闕專祀，諭言：「虞書六宗，漢儒釋為乾坤六子，震雷、巽風，並列禋祀。

translations.literal: The next year, because exclusive worship of the Cloud Master and Thunder Master was still lacking, an edict stated: "The Six Honored Ones in the Book of Yu—Han scholars interpreted them as the six sons of Heaven and Earth; Thunder of the Zhen trigram and Wind of the Xun trigram are equally ranked in solemn sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, noting that the Cloud Master and Thunder Master still lacked dedicated worship, an edict declared: "The Six Honored Ones in the Book of Yu—Han scholars read them as the six offspring of Heaven and Earth. Thunder of the Zhen trigram and Wind of the Xun trigram stand equally among the highest sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 易言雷動風散，功實相等。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes speaks of thunder stirring and wind dispersing—their efficacy is truly equal.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says thunder moves and wind scatters—their powers are truly equal.

sentences.zh: 記曰：『天降時雨，山川出雲。』

translations.literal: The Record says: 'Heaven sends timely rain; mountains and rivers produce clouds.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record states: 'Heaven sends timely rain; mountains and rivers give forth clouds.'

sentences.zh: 周禮以雲物辨年歲，是雲與雷皆運行造化者也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou use cloud formations to distinguish the year's harvest; thus both cloud and thunder are agents that operate the creative transformation of nature.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou read the seasons in clouds and sky-signs; cloud and thunder alike are the workings of creation itself.

sentences.zh: 並官建廟奉祀。」

translations.literal: Both likewise had temples erected by the court and received dedicated worship."
translations.idiomatic: Temples were built for both at court, and worship was established."

sentences.zh: 於是下所司議，尋奏：「唐天寶五載，增祀雷師，位雨師次，歲以立夏後申日致祭，宋、元因之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation; they soon memorialized: "In the fifth year of Tianbao of Tang, sacrifice to the Thunder Master was added, his place below the Rain Master; each year sacrifice was performed on the shen day after the Beginning of Summer; Song and Yuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the appropriate offices; they soon reported: "In Tang Tianbao 5, worship of the Thunder Master was added, ranked below the Rain Master, with annual sacrifice on the shen day after Start of Summer; Song and Yuan retained this practice.

sentences.zh: 明集禮，次風師以雲師，郡、縣建雷雨、風雲二壇，秋分後三日合祭。

translations.literal: The Ming Collected Ritual ranked the Cloud Master next after the Wind Master; at the commandery and county level two altars were erected for Thunder-and-Rain and Wind-and-Cloud, with combined sacrifice three days after the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming Collected Ritual, the Cloud Master followed the Wind Master; commanderies and counties built twin altars for thunder-and-rain and for wind-and-cloud, offering combined sacrifice three days after the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 今擬西方建雷師廟，祭以立夏後申日。

translations.literal: It is now proposed to build a Thunder Master temple in the west, with sacrifice on the shen day after the Beginning of Summer.
translations.idiomatic: The plan is to erect a Thunder Master temple in the west, with sacrifice on the shen day after Start of Summer.

sentences.zh: 東方建雲師廟，祭以秋分後三日。」

translations.literal: In the east to build a Cloud Master temple, with sacrifice three days after the autumn equinox."
translations.idiomatic: In the east a Cloud Master temple is to be built, with sacrifice three days after the autumn equinox."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 乃錫號雲師曰「順時普應」，廟曰凝和；

translations.literal: Then honorific titles were bestowed: the Cloud Master was titled "Compliant with the Seasons and Universally Responsive," his temple named Ninghe;
translations.idiomatic: Titles were then granted: the Cloud Master was styled "Compliant with the Seasons and Universally Responsive," his temple called Ninghe;

sentences.zh: 雷師曰「資生髮育」，廟曰昭顯；

translations.literal: the Thunder Master was titled "Nourishing Life and Generating Growth," his temple named Zhaoxian;
translations.idiomatic: the Thunder Master "Nourishing Life and Fostering Growth," his temple Zhaoxian;

sentences.zh: 並以時應宮龍神為雨師，合祀之。

translations.literal: and together with the Dragon Spirit of the Shiying Palace as Rain Master, they were worshipped jointly.
translations.idiomatic: together with the Dragon Spirit of the Shiying Palace serving as Rain Master, all were worshipped as one rite.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年旱，禱雨既應，仁宗蒞壇報祀，入壇中門降輿，至壝南門外，盥畢入，升壇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing there was drought; after prayer for rain was answered, the Renzong Emperor came to the altar in thanksgiving sacrifice; entering the altar's central gate he descended from the carriage, reached outside the southern gate of the circumvallation, after ablutions entered, and ascended the altar.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2, during drought, rain answered prayer; the Renzong Emperor came to the altar to offer thanks. He entered through the central gate and alighted, proceeded to outside the southern circumvallation gate, performed ablutions, entered, and ascended the altar.

sentences.zh: 以次詣雲、雨、風、雷神位上香，二跪六拜。

translations.literal: In order he proceeded to the seats of Cloud, Rain, Wind, and Thunder to burn incense, with two kneelings and six prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: In turn he burned incense at the seats of the Cloud, Rain, Wind, and Thunder spirits, kneeling twice and bowing six times.

sentences.zh: 初獻即奠爵、帛，讀祝，不晉俎，不飲福胙。

translations.literal: At the first presentation he immediately set out libation cups and silk, read the invocation, but did not advance the sacrificial trays, and did not partake of the blessing meat.
translations.idiomatic: At the first offering he presented cups and silk and read the invocation, but omitted advancing the meat trays and partaking of the blessed sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 餘如故。

translations.literal: The rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the usual rite.

sentences.zh: 太歲殿位先農壇東北，正殿祀太歲，兩廡祀十二月將。

translations.literal: The Grand Year Hall stood northeast of the Spirit of Agriculture Altar; the main hall enshrined the Grand Year, the two side galleries the Twelve Monthly Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Year Hall stood northeast of the Altar of the Spirit of Agriculture; the Grand Year was worshipped in the main hall, the Twelve Monthly Commanders in the side galleries.

sentences.zh: 順治初，遣官祭太歲，定孟春為迎，歲暮為祖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, officials were dispatched to sacrifice to the Grand Year; the first month of spring was fixed for receiving him, year's end for seeing him off.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, officials were sent to sacrifice to the Grand Year; the first month of spring was fixed for welcoming him, year's end for sending him off.

sentences.zh: 歲正月，書神牌曰「某干支太歲神」，如其年建。

translations.literal: Each first month of the year, the spirit tablet was inscribed "Grand Year Spirit of such-and-such stem-and-branch," according to the year's cyclical designation.
translations.idiomatic: Each first month the spirit tablet was inscribed "Grand Year Spirit of the year's stem-and-branch designation," matching the year's cyclical sign.

sentences.zh: 歲除祭畢，合祝版燎之。

translations.literal: When the year's-end sacrifice was completed, the prayer boards were gathered and burned.
translations.idiomatic: After the year's-end sacrifice, the prayer boards were collected and burned.

sentences.zh: 凡祭，樂六奏，承祭官立中階下，分獻官立甬道左右，行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: For each sacrifice, music was performed six times; the officiating official stood below the middle steps, collateral-presenting officials to left and right of the central walkway, performing the rite of three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: At each sacrifice six musical performances were given; the principal officiant stood below the middle terrace, collateral presenters flanked the central path, and all performed three kneelings and nine bows.

sentences.zh: 初獻即奠帛，讀祝，錫福胙，用樂舞生承事，時猶無上香儀也。

translations.literal: At the first presentation he immediately offered silk, read the invocation, bestowed blessing meat, and musicians and dancers performed service—at that time there was as yet no incense-burning rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the first offering silk was presented and the invocation read; blessed sacrificial meat was distributed and musicians and dancers performed—incense had not yet been added to the rite.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，禮臣言同屬天神，不宜有異，自是二祭及分獻皆上香。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, ritual officials stated that as these belonged equally to the celestial spirits, they ought not to differ; from then on both sacrifices and collateral presentation included incense.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 16, ritual officials argued that since these rites belonged to the same order of celestial spirits, they should not differ; from then on incense was burned at both the main and collateral offerings.

sentences.zh: 太歲、月將神牌，舊儲農壇神庫，至是亦以殿廡具備，移奉正屋。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of the Grand Year and Monthly Commanders had formerly been stored in the Agriculture Altar spirit repository; by this time, with the hall and galleries fully equipped, they were moved and enshrined in the main building.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets for the Grand Year and Monthly Commanders had previously been kept in the agriculture altar's spirit vault; now, with hall and galleries complete, they were moved to the main building.

sentences.zh: 臨祭，龕前安神座。

translations.literal: On the eve of sacrifice, spirit thrones were set before the niches.
translations.idiomatic: Before sacrifice, spirit thrones were placed before the niches.

sentences.zh: 畢，復龕。

translations.literal: When finished, they were returned to the niches.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was done, they were returned to the niches.

sentences.zh: 舊制，祭太歲遣太常卿行禮，兩廡用廳員分獻。

translations.literal: Under the old system, sacrifice to the Grand Year was performed by the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the two galleries by clerks of the office as collateral presenters.
translations.idiomatic: Under the earlier rule, the Grand Year sacrifice was conducted by the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with office clerks presenting at the two side galleries.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改遣親王、郡王承祭。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, imperial princes and commandery princes were appointed to perform the rite instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, princes and commandery princes were assigned to officiate.

sentences.zh: 次年，定太常卿為分獻官。

translations.literal: The following year the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was fixed as collateral presenter.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the ritual director was designated collateral presenter.

sentences.zh: 雍、乾以來，凡祈禱，天神、太歲暨地祇三壇並舉，遣官將事，陪祀者咸與焉。

translations.literal: From the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns onward, for all prayer rites the Celestial Spirits, Grand Year, and Earth Spirits altars were all conducted together, with dispatched officials conducting the affairs and all who accompanied the sacrifice taking part.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongzheng and Qianlong onward, prayer rites were held jointly at the altars of the Celestial Spirits, Grand Year, and Earth Spirits; dispatched officials conducted the rites and all attendant worshippers participated.

sentences.zh: 前期邸齋一日，承祭官拜位。

translations.literal: One day beforehand abstinence was kept at the lodge, the officiating official at his bowing place.
translations.idiomatic: One day prior, abstinence was observed at the lodge and the principal officiant took his place for obeisance.

sentences.zh: 天神壇在南階下，太歲與常祀同，俱三跪九拜。

translations.literal: The Celestial Spirits altar was below the southern steps; the Grand Year rite was the same as the regular sacrifice, both with three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Spirits altar stood below the southern terrace; the Grand Year rite matched the regular sacrifice—three kneelings and nine bows throughout.

sentences.zh: 天神用燎，太歲兩廡不分獻，不飲福、受胙。

translations.literal: For the Celestial Spirits burning offering was used; for the Grand Year the two galleries had no separate collateral presentation, and neither drinking the blessing nor receiving sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Spirits rite employed burnt offerings; at the Grand Year altar the side galleries received no separate presentations, and the blessing meat was neither consumed nor received.

sentences.zh: 朝日、夕月，初以大明、夜明從祀圜丘，罷春秋分祀。

translations.literal: The Morning Sun and Evening Moon, at first with Great Brightness and Night Brightness as collateral at the Round Mound, the spring and autumn separate sacrifices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Morning Sun and Evening Moon worship began with Great Brightness and Night Brightness offered collaterally at the Round Mound; the separate spring and autumn sacrifices were later discontinued.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，建朝日壇東郊，夕月壇西郊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, the Morning Sun altar was built in the eastern suburb, the Evening Moon altar in the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8, the Morning Sun altar was erected in the eastern suburbs and the Evening Moon altar in the western suburbs.

sentences.zh: 朝日用春分日卯刻，值甲、丙、戊、庚、壬年，帝親祭，餘遣官。

translations.literal: The Morning Sun sacrifice was performed at the mao hour on the day of the spring equinox; in years of jia, bing, wu, geng, and ren the emperor sacrificed in person, otherwise officials were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Morning Sun sacrifice fell at the mao hour on the spring equinox; in jia, bing, wu, geng, and ren years the emperor officiated in person, in other years officials were sent.

sentences.zh: 樂六奏，舞八佾。

translations.literal: Music was performed six times, dance with eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: Six musical pieces were performed and an eight-row dance was offered.

sentences.zh: 凡親祭，入自壇北門，至甬道更衣大次，盥畢，升西階就位，行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, he entered by the altar's northern gate, reached the central walk to the great changing pavilion, after ablutions ascended the western steps to take his place, performing the rite of three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor officiated in person, he entered through the northern gate, proceeded along the central path to the great robing pavilion, performed ablutions, ascended the western steps to his place, and offered three kneelings and nine bows.

sentences.zh: 奠獻遣有司行。

translations.literal: Presentation and offering were performed by dispatched officials.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings were presented by dispatched officials.

sentences.zh: 遣代則行禮階下，惟讀祝時跽壇上。

translations.literal: When an official was dispatched as substitute he performed the rite below the steps, only kneeling on the altar when reading the invocation.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy substituted, the rite was performed at the foot of the steps; only when reading the invocation did he kneel on the altar.

sentences.zh: 初日壇用露祭。

translations.literal: At first the Sun altar used open-air sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Sun altar employed open-air sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，始援社稷例，立龕壇下芘風雨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, following the precedent of the Soil and Grain, a niche was set beneath the altar to shelter from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4, following the Soil and Grain precedent, a sheltered niche was installed beneath the altar against wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十一年，具服殿成，罷更衣大次。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Qianlong, when the Vestment Hall was completed, the great changing pavilion was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 11, with completion of the Vestment Hall, the great robing pavilion was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 是歲春分翼日日食，高宗蒞祭，不乘輦，不奏樂，不陳鹵簿。

translations.literal: That year on the yi day of the spring equinox there was a solar eclipse; the Gaozong Emperor came to sacrifice, not riding the carriage, not performing music, not displaying the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: That year a solar eclipse fell on the spring equinox; the Gaozong Emperor attended sacrifice without carriage, music, or imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 三十九年躬祭，入霝星左門，如幄次行禮，以年高酌減禮文，非恆式也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he sacrificed in person, entering the Lingxing Left Gate, performing the rite as at a pavilion—due to advanced age the ritual was appropriately reduced; this was not the constant form.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he officiated in person, entering through the Lingxing Left Gate and performing the abbreviated pavilion rite; the ceremony was modestly reduced on account of his age and was not the standing precedent.

sentences.zh: 夕月用秋分日酉刻，奉星辰配，凡丑、辰、未、戌年，帝親祭，餘遣官。

translations.literal: The Evening Moon sacrifice was performed at the you hour on the day of the autumn equinox, with stars as collateral; in years of chou, chen, wei, and xu the emperor sacrificed in person, otherwise officials were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Evening Moon sacrifice was held at the you hour on the autumn equinox, with the stars offered collaterally; in chou, chen, wei, and xu years the emperor officiated in person, otherwise officials were sent.

sentences.zh: 樂六奏，儀視日壇稍殺，親臨較少。

translations.literal: Music was performed six times; the rite was somewhat reduced compared with the Sun altar, and personal attendance was less frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Six musical pieces were performed; the ceremony was slightly simpler than at the Sun altar, and the emperor attended less often.

sentences.zh: 升壇行禮，二跪六拜，初獻奠玉帛，讀祝，餘如朝日儀。

translations.literal: Ascending the altar to perform the rite: two kneelings and six prostrations; at the first presentation jade and silk were offered, the invocation read; the rest followed the Morning Sun rite.
translations.idiomatic: On ascending the altar: two kneelings and six bows; at the first offering jade and silk were presented and the invocation read; the remainder followed the Morning Sun rite.

sentences.zh: 遣官則拜壇下。

translations.literal: When officials were dispatched they bowed below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched officials bowed at the foot of the altar.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年戊午，例遣官，帝因初舉祀典，仍親祭如禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, wuwu year, by precedent officials were to be dispatched, but because this was the first performance of the sacrificial canon the emperor still sacrificed in person according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 (wuwu), officials were dispatched by precedent, yet because this was the inaugural observance of the canon the emperor still officiated in person.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，酌損節文，如日壇例。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, the ritual details were appropriately reduced, following the Sun altar precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year the ceremony was modestly simplified, following the Sun altar precedent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年庚申，效高宗故事，仍親祭，不遣官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, gengshen year, following the Gaozong Emperor's precedent, he still sacrificed in person, not dispatching officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 (gengshen), emulating the Gaozong Emperor's example, he again officiated in person without sending officials.

sentences.zh: 十九年，定親祭儀，祀配位用親王、郡王上香。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the personal sacrifice rite was fixed: at collateral seats imperial princes and commandery princes burned incense.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the personal-officiant rite was fixed: princes and commandery princes burned incense at the collateral seats.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，世宗忌日值月壇齋期，諭陪祀執事官改常服，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Shizong Emperor's death anniversary fell on the Moon altar abstinence period; an edict ordered attending and officiating officials to wear ordinary dress; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the Shizong Emperor's death anniversary coincided with Moon-altar abstinence; attendant and officiating officials were ordered to wear ordinary dress; all else remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 社稷之祀自京師以至直省府、州、縣皆有之，其在京師者，建壇端門右。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Soil and Grain existed from the capital to every province, prefecture, commandery, and county; in the capital the altar was built to the right of the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soil and Grain sacrifice extended from the capital to every province, prefecture, and county; in Beijing the altar stood to the right of the Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 世祖宅帝位，祭告如儀。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the imperial throne, he made sacrificial announcement according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor assumed the throne, he performed the sacrificial announcement as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 定制，歲春、秋仲月上戊日，祭大社、大稷，奉后土句龍氏、后稷氏配。

translations.literal: It was fixed that on the wu day of the second month of spring and autumn each year, Great Soil and Great Grain were sacrificed to, with Hou Tu Goulong and Hou Ji as collateral.
translations.idiomatic: By fixed rule, on the wu days of the second months of spring and autumn, Great Soil and Great Grain were worshipped, with Hou Tu Goulong and Hou Ji offered collaterally.

sentences.zh: 祭日，帝親蒞，壇上敷五色土，各如其方。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice the emperor came in person; on the altar five-colored earth was spread, each according to its direction.
translations.idiomatic: On sacrifice day the emperor attended in person; five-colored earth was spread on the altar, each hue matching its direction.

sentences.zh: 樂七奏，舞八佾。

translations.literal: Music was performed seven times, dance with eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: Seven musical pieces were performed with an eight-row dance.

sentences.zh: 帝出闕右門降輦，道北門出入，祭時出拜殿，至壝北門外就位，自北階升壇上香，詣正位奠獻。

translations.literal: The emperor exited through the Que Right Gate and descended from the carriage, went out and in by the northern way; at sacrifice time he exited the bowing hall, reached outside the northern gate of the circumvallation to take his place, ascended by the northern steps to burn incense, and proceeded to the principal seat to present offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left through the Que Right Gate and alighted, entering and exiting by the northern route; at the hour of sacrifice he emerged from the bowing hall, took his place outside the northern circumvallation gate, ascended the northern steps to burn incense, and presented offerings at the principal seat.

sentences.zh: 有司分祭配位。

translations.literal: Officials separately sacrificed at the collateral seats.
translations.idiomatic: Officials conducted the collateral offerings.

sentences.zh: 升北階，降西階，不晉俎，三跪九拜。

translations.literal: Ascending by the northern steps, descending by the western steps, not advancing the sacrificial trays, three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the northern steps and descended the western steps, omitting advancement of the meat trays, and performed three kneelings and nine bows.

sentences.zh: 餘儀如北郊舊例。

translations.literal: The rest of the rite followed the old precedent of the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the former northern-suburb precedent.

sentences.zh: 祭日逢國忌，不改期，易素服。

translations.literal: If the day of sacrifice coincided with a dynastic mourning anniversary, the date was not changed; plain dress was worn.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice day fell on a dynastic mourning anniversary, the date was unchanged but plain dress was worn.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，遇太宗忌日，始改中戊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, when it fell on Taizong's death anniversary, it was moved for the first time to the middle wu day.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3, when the rite coincided with Taizong's death anniversary, the sacrifice was shifted for the first time to the middle wu day.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，平青海，告祭行獻俘禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, when Qinghai was pacified, announcement sacrifice was performed with the captive presentation rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2, upon pacifying Qinghai, a victory announcement was made with the presentation-of-captives rite.

sentences.zh: 自是平定籓部，獻俘以為常。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever frontier regions were pacified, captive presentation became regular.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever border territories were pacified, presentation of captives became standard.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，改送燎為望瘞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong, sending the burnt offering was changed to distant burial.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17, the sending-off of burnt offerings was changed to distant interment.

sentences.zh: 明年，增望瘞樂章。

translations.literal: The following year, music for distant burial was added.
translations.idiomatic: The next year musical pieces were added for the distant-interment rite.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以年老更儀節。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, due to advanced age the ritual procedure was altered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year the ceremony was modified on account of the emperor's advanced age.

sentences.zh: 幄次先設拜殿，帝御輦至壇外門，易禮輿，入右門，至拜殿東階下，乃降。

translations.literal: At the pavilion a bowing hall was set first; the emperor rode the carriage to the altar's outer gate, changed to the ritual sedan, entered the right gate, reached the eastern steps below the bowing hall, and then descended.
translations.idiomatic: A bowing hall was prepared at the pavilion first; the emperor rode to the altar's outer gate, switched to the ritual sedan, entered the right gate, and alighted at the eastern steps of the bowing hall.

sentences.zh: 升階行禮，禮成，升輿如初。

translations.literal: He ascended the steps to perform the rite; when the rite was complete, he mounted the sedan as before.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended to perform the rite, and when it was complete remounted the sedan as before.

sentences.zh: 故事，祭日遇風雨，拜位香案徙殿中，神位祭品露設如故。

translations.literal: By precedent, if on sacrifice day wind and rain came, the bowing place and incense table were moved into the hall, while spirit seats and sacrificial objects remained set in the open as before.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when wind or rain fell on sacrifice day, the bowing place and incense table were moved into the hall while spirit seats and offerings remained exposed outdoors.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「社稷之制，不立棟宇，以承天陽。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The institution of Soil and Grain does not erect buildings, so as to receive heaven's yang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Soil and Grain institution erects no buildings, so as to receive heaven's yang.

sentences.zh: 今神牌藏神庫，是在棟宇內也。

translations.literal: Now the spirit tablets are stored in the spirit repository—that is within a building.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the spirit tablets are kept in the spirit vault—that is already within a building.

sentences.zh: 移奉殿中，復何嫌忌？」

translations.literal: To move them and enshrine them in the hall—what further scruple is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Moving them into the hall—what objection remains?"

sentences.zh: 四十一年，定祭日遇風雨，神牌安奉殿內，祭器、樂虡移設拜殿，猝遇則用木龕覆神牌，其拜殿別設香案。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year it was fixed: when wind and rain came on sacrifice day, spirit tablets were installed inside the hall, sacrificial vessels and music stands were moved to the bowing hall; if rain came suddenly wooden niches covered the spirit tablets, and the bowing hall had a separate incense table.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year the rule was fixed: on rainy sacrifice days spirit tablets were housed in the hall, vessels and music stands were relocated to the bowing hall; if rain came suddenly wooden niches covered the tablets, and a separate incense table was set in the bowing hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，仁宗詣壇祈雨，視春秋致祭儀，惟祭品用脯醢、果實，不飲福。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, the Renzong Emperor went to the altar to pray for rain, following the spring and autumn sacrifice rite, only with dried and pickled meats and fruits as sacrificial objects, not drinking the blessing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 the Renzong Emperor prayed for rain at the altar, following the spring and autumn sacrifice rite but offering only dried and pickled meats and fruits, without partaking of the blessed sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 前三日及祭日，王、公、百官皆齋戒，禁屠宰，不理刑名。

translations.literal: Three days before and on the day of sacrifice, princes, nobles, and all officials kept abstinence, slaughter was forbidden, and judicial matters were not handled.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before and on sacrifice day, princes, nobles, and officials observed abstinence; slaughter was forbidden and legal matters suspended.

sentences.zh: 餘悉如故。

translations.literal: Everything else was entirely as before.
translations.idiomatic: All else remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 並諭親詣祈禱、報祀均步行，以隆典禮。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that when going in person to pray or offer thanksgiving sacrifice one should walk on foot, to elevate the solemnity of the rite.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also required that personal attendance for prayer and thanksgiving be on foot, to honor the solemnity of the rite.

sentences.zh: 其在府、州、縣者，順治元年建，歲祭亦用上戊，府稱府社、府稷，州、縣則雲某州、縣社、稷。

translations.literal: Those at the prefecture, commandery, and county level were built in the first year of Shunzhi; yearly sacrifice likewise used the upper wu day; at the prefecture level they were called Prefecture Soil and Prefecture Grain; at commandery and county they were called such-and-such Commandery or County Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Local altars at prefecture, commandery, and county level were built in Shunzhi 1; annual sacrifice likewise used the first wu day; prefectures called theirs Prefecture Soil and Grain, while commanderies and counties named them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 世宗纘業，制定祭品，羊一，豕一，帛一、籩、豆四，鉶、簠、簋各二。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor succeeded, sacrificial objects were fixed: one sheep, one pig, one piece of silk, four baskets and four cups, two tureens each of ting, fu, and gui.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shizong Emperor the offerings were standardized: one sheep, one pig, one bolt of silk, four baskets and four cups, and two each of ting, fu, and gui vessels.

sentences.zh: 有司齋二日，屆期朝服祭於壇。

translations.literal: Officials kept abstinence two days; when the day arrived they wore court dress and sacrificed at the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Officials observed two days of abstinence and, on the appointed day, sacrificed at the altar in court dress.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，始頒祝文，各直省定例，為民祈報，會城布政使主之，督若撫陪祀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, invocation texts were first issued; each province had fixed rules; praying and giving thanks for the people—the provincial treasurer at the capital presided, governor or governor-general accompanying the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8 invocation texts were first promulgated; each province received fixed rules. For prayers and thanksgiving on the people's behalf the provincial treasurer at the capital presided, with the governor or governor-general in attendance.

sentences.zh: 道官駐地，府、州、縣主之，道陪祀。

translations.literal: Where circuit officials were stationed, prefectures, commanderies, and counties presided, circuit officials accompanying the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Where circuit intendant offices were stationed, local prefectures and counties presided with the circuit intendant in attendance.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以尊卑未協，詔互易之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because rank order was not appropriate, an edict ordered them exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, because rank order was incongruous, an edict swapped their roles.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、道官或出巡，仍令布政使暨府、州、縣官攝祭。

translations.literal: If governors, governor-generals, or circuit officials were away on inspection, the provincial treasurer together with prefecture, commandery, and county officials still officiated as substitutes.
translations.idiomatic: If governors or circuit officials were on tour, the provincial treasurer and local officials still officiated in their stead.

sentences.zh: 武官自將軍以下，皆陪祀。

translations.literal: Military officials from general downward all accompanied the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers from the rank of general down all attended the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 社、稷以次諸祭，悉准此行。

translations.literal: Soil and Grain and all subsequent sacrifices entirely followed this conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Soil and Grain and all related local sacrifices followed this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 先農天聰九年，禁濫役妨農。

translations.literal: Spirit of Agriculture: In the ninth year of Tiancong, corvée labor that harmed farming was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit of Agriculture: In Tiancong 9, abusive corvée that impeded farming was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，禁屯積米穀，令及時耕種，重農貴粟自此始。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, hoarding grain was forbidden, timely planting and cultivation were ordered—the esteem for agriculture and grain began from this.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 hoarding grain was forbidden and timely planting enforced—emphasis on agriculture and grain began here.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，定歲仲春亥日行耕耤禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, the plowing-and-weeding rite was fixed for the hai day of the second month of spring each year.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 the sacred plowing rite was fixed for the hai day of mid-spring each year.

sentences.zh: 先期，戶、禮二部尚書偕順天府尹進耒耜暨穜棱種。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the ministers of Revenue and Rites together with the Shuntian prefect advanced the plow and hoe and various seed grains.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand, the ministers of Revenue and Rites together with the Shuntian prefect presented the plow, hoe, and assorted seed grains.

sentences.zh: 屆期，帝親饗祭獻如朝日儀。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, the emperor personally performed the feasting sacrifice and presentation according to the Morning Sun rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor personally conducted the sacrificial feast and offerings as at the Morning Sun rite.

sentences.zh: 畢，詣耕耤所，南鄉立。

translations.literal: When finished, he proceeded to the plowing-and-weeding ground and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was complete, he proceeded to the plowing ground and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 從耤者就位。

translations.literal: Those who accompanied the plowing took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Those joining the plowing took their positions.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書執耒耜，府尹執鞭，北面跪以進。

translations.literal: The minister of Revenue held the plow and hoe, the prefect held the whip, both kneeling facing north to present them.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of Revenue bore the plow and hoe, the prefect the whip; kneeling to the north, they presented them.

sentences.zh: 帝秉耒三推，府丞奉青箱，戶部侍郎播種，耆老隨覆。

translations.literal: The emperor took the plow and pushed three furrows; the prefectural vice-director held the green seed box, the vice-minister of Revenue sowed, and elders followed covering the seed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the plow and pushed three furrows; the vice-prefect held the green seed box, the vice-minister of Revenue scattered seed, and elders followed to cover it.

sentences.zh: 畢，尚書受耒耜，府尹受鞭。

translations.literal: When finished, the minister received back the plow and hoe, the prefect the whip.
translations.idiomatic: When done, the minister received back the plow and hoe and the prefect the whip.

sentences.zh: 帝御觀耕台，南鄉坐，王以下序立。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the Viewing-Plow terrace, sat facing south, and princes and below stood in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat on the Viewing-Plow terrace facing south; princes and those below stood in ranked order.

sentences.zh: 三王五推，九卿九推，府尹官屬執青箱播種，耆老隨覆。

translations.literal: Three princes pushed five furrows, the Nine Ministers nine furrows; prefectural staff held the green seed box and sowed, elders following to cover.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes pushed five furrows each, the Nine Ministers nine each; prefectural staff scattered seed from the green boxes while elders followed to cover.

sentences.zh: 畢，帝如齋宮。

translations.literal: When finished, the emperor went to the abstention palace.
translations.idiomatic: When this was done, the emperor went to the abstention palace.

sentences.zh: 府尹官屬、眾耆老行禮。

translations.literal: The prefectural intendant's subordinates and all the elders performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The intendant's staff and the assembled elders performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 農夫三十人執農器隨行。

translations.literal: Thirty farmers bearing farm implements followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty farmers carrying farming tools followed in procession.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，從府、縣官出至耕耤所，帝賜王公坐，俟農夫終畝，鴻臚卿奏禮成，百官行慶賀禮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, following the prefectural and county officials out to the sacred plowing ground, the emperor granted seats to the princes and nobles, waited for the farmers to finish the field, the director of the Court of State Ceremonial reported completion, and the officials performed the congratulatory rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, he followed the prefectural and county officials out to the sacred plowing field, granted seats to the princes and nobles, and waited while the farmers completed the furrow; the director of the Court of State Ceremonial announced that the rite was complete, and the officials performed the congratulatory ceremony.

sentences.zh: 賜王公耆老宴，賞農夫布各一匹，作樂還宮。

translations.literal: He granted a banquet to the princes, nobles, and elders, rewarded each farmer with one bolt of cloth, and returned to the palace with music.
translations.idiomatic: He gave a feast to the princes, nobles, and elders, rewarded each farmer with a bolt of cloth, and returned to the palace to music.

sentences.zh: 其秋，年穀登，所司上聞，擇日貯神倉，備供粢盛。

translations.literal: That autumn, when the year's grain ripened, the responsible offices reported upward, chose a day to store it in the spirit granary, and prepared it to supply sacrificial grain.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when the year's harvest came in, the responsible offices reported to the throne, chose a day to store grain in the spirit granary, and set it aside for sacrificial offerings.

sentences.zh: 尋定先農歲祭遣府尹行，大興、宛平縣官陪祀。

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed that for the annual sacrifice to the Spirit of the First Farmer the prefectural intendant would officiate, with officials of Daxing and Wanping counties joining as collateral worshippers.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon ordained that the annual sacrifice to the Spirit of the First Farmer would be conducted by the prefectural intendant, with officials of Daxing and Wanping counties attending as collateral worshippers.

sentences.zh: 唐熙時，聖祖嘗臨豐澤園勸相。

translations.literal: In the Tangxi era, the Sage Ancestor once went to Fengze Garden to encourage farming.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tangxi reign, the Sage Ancestor had on occasion visited Fengze Garden to encourage plowing.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，祭先農，行耕耤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, he sacrificed to the Spirit of the First Farmer and performed sacred plowing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng, he sacrificed to the Spirit of the First Farmer and performed the sacred plowing rite.

sentences.zh: 三推畢，加一推。

translations.literal: When the three plowings were complete, one more was added.
translations.idiomatic: After the three ritual plowings, he added a fourth.

sentences.zh: 頒新制三十六禾詞。

translations.literal: He issued the newly composed thirty-six grain verses.
translations.idiomatic: He promulgated the newly composed thirty-six verses on the grains.

sentences.zh: 賞農夫布各四匹，罷筵宴。

translations.literal: He rewarded each farmer with four bolts of cloth and discontinued the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded each farmer with four bolts of cloth and dispensed with the feast.

sentences.zh: 頒賜各省嘉禾圖。

translations.literal: He issued and bestowed illustrated auspicious-grain charts to each province.
translations.idiomatic: He issued and bestowed illustrated charts of auspicious grain to every province.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，帝初行耕耤禮，先期六日，幸豐澤園演耕，屆日饗先農，行四推。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, when the emperor first performed the sacred plowing rite, six days beforehand he visited Fengze Garden to rehearse plowing; on the appointed day he offered to the Spirit of the First Farmer and performed four plowings.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong, when the emperor first performed the sacred plowing rite, he visited Fengze Garden six days beforehand to rehearse the plowing; on the appointed day he offered to the Spirit of the First Farmer and performed four ritual plowings.

sentences.zh: 二十三年諭曰：「吉亥耤畝，所重劭農。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year an edict said: "The auspicious hai day sacred field plowing emphasizes encouraging agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year an edict said: "The sacred plowing on the auspicious hai day is meant above all to encourage farming.

sentences.zh: 黛耜青箱，畚鎛蓑笠，咸寓知民疾苦至意。

translations.literal: The dark plow, green seed box, basket, hoe, rain cape, and bamboo hat all embody the utmost intent to know the people's toil.
translations.idiomatic: The dark plow, green seed box, basket, hoe, rain cape, and bamboo hat all embody the utmost concern to understand the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 吾民雨犁日耘，襏襫維艱，炎濕遑避。

translations.literal: Our people plow in rain and hoe by day; their coarse garments speak of hardship; in heat and damp they have no leisure to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Our people plow in rain and weed by day; in their coarse garments they know only hardship, and in heat or damp they have no respite.

sentences.zh: 設棚懸彩，義無所取。

translations.literal: To set up canopies and hang colored silks has no legitimate meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Erecting canopies and hanging colored silks serves no legitimate purpose.

sentences.zh: 且片時所用，費中人數十戶產也，其除之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, what is used for a short while costs the property of dozens of middle-class households—remove it."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what is used for a few hours costs as much as the estates of dozens of ordinary households—abolish it."

sentences.zh: 三十七年，群臣慮帝春秋高，籥罷親耕，不許。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year the assembled ministers, concerned that the emperor's years were advanced, proposed discontinuing personal plowing, but permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year the ministers, fearing that the emperor had grown old, proposed ending his personal plowing, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 命仍依古制三推。

translations.literal: He ordered that the ancient practice of three plowings still be followed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that the ancient practice of three ritual plowings be retained.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以降，仍加一推如初。

translations.literal: From Jiaqing onward, one additional plowing was again added as at first.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jiaqing reign onward, one additional plowing was again added, as before.

sentences.zh: 直省祭先農，清初未舉行。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Spirit of the First Farmer in the provinces was not performed in the early Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial sacrifices to the Spirit of the First Farmer were not performed in the early Qing.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，耤田產嘉禾，一莖三四穗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, the sacred field produced auspicious grain with three or four ears on one stalk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng, the sacred field produced auspicious grain bearing three or four ears on a single stalk.

sentences.zh: 越二年，乃至九穗。

translations.literal: Two years later it reached nine ears.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later it bore as many as nine ears.

sentences.zh: 諭言：「國以民為本，民以食為天。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The state takes the people as its foundation; the people take food as their heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The state rests on its people, and the people rest on food.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子耤千畝，諸侯百畝。

translations.literal: In ritual, the Son of Heaven plows a thousand mu; feudal lords a hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, the Son of Heaven plows a thousand mu; feudal lords plow a hundred mu.

sentences.zh: 是耕耤可通臣下，守土者允宜遵行。

translations.literal: Thus sacred plowing may be extended to ministers and subordinates; those who guard the soil ought indeed to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred plowing, then, ought to extend to officials below the throne, and local administrators should follow it.

sentences.zh: 俾知稼牆艱難，察地力肥磽，量天時晴雨。

translations.literal: So that they may know the hardship of sowing and reaping, observe whether the soil is fertile or poor, and gauge the season's rain and sun.
translations.idiomatic: So that they may understand the hardship of sowing and reaping, assess whether the land is rich or poor, and heed the season's weather.

sentences.zh: 養民務本，道實由之。」

translations.literal: To nourish the people and honor the fundamental—this is truly the way."
translations.idiomatic: Nourishing the people and honoring the root of rule—this is truly the path."

sentences.zh: 於是定議：順天府尹，直省督撫及所屬府、州、縣、衛，各立農壇耤田。

translations.literal: Thereupon deliberation fixed: the Shuntian prefectural intendant, provincial governors-general and governors and their subordinate prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons each established an agriculture altar and sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was ordained that the Shuntian intendant, provincial governors-general and governors, and their subordinate prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons should each establish an agriculture altar and sacred plowing field.

sentences.zh: 自五年始，歲仲春亥日，率屬祭先農行九推。

translations.literal: From the fifth year onward, on the hai day of the middle spring month each year, leading their subordinates they sacrificed to the Spirit of the First Farmer and performed nine plowings.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth year onward, on the hai day of mid-spring each year, they would lead their subordinates in sacrificing to the Spirit of the First Farmer and performing nine ritual plowings.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，頒時憲書，豫定次年耕耤吉期，下所司循用。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month they issued the calendar, predetermined the auspicious date for the next year's sacred plowing, and sent it down to the responsible offices for observance.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month they issued the official calendar, predetermined the auspicious date for the next year's sacred plowing, and sent it to the responsible offices for compliance.

sentences.zh: 祭品禮數，如社稷儀。

translations.literal: Sacrificial offerings and ritual procedure were as at the State Altars.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial offerings and ritual procedure followed the State Altars precedent.

sentences.zh: 先蠶清初未列祀典。

translations.literal: The Spirit of the First Silkworm was not listed in the sacrificial canon in the early Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Spirit of the First Silkworm was not included in the sacrificial canon in the early Qing.

sentences.zh: 康熙時，立蠶舍豐澤園，始興蠶績。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era, silkworm houses were established in Fengze Garden, and sericulture was first undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, silkworm houses were established in Fengze Garden, and sericulture was first undertaken.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，河東總督王士俊疏請祀先蠶，略言：「周禮鄭註上引房星，以馬神為蠶神。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, the governor-general of Hedong Wang Shijun memorialized requesting sacrifice to the Spirit of the First Silkworm, stating in summary: "In the commentaries on the Zhou Rites, Zheng Xuan cites the Room Star above and takes the Horse Spirit as the silkworm spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Hedong governor-general Wang Shijun memorialized requesting sacrifice to the Spirit of the First Silkworm, noting in summary: "In Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Zhou Rites, the Room Star is cited above and the Horse Spirit is taken as the silkworm deity.

sentences.zh: 蠶、馬同出天駟，然天駟可雲馬祖，實非蠶神。

translations.literal: Silkworm and horse both emerge from the Celestial Quarters, yet the Celestial Quarters may be called the Horse Ancestor and are not in fact the silkworm spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm and horse both derive from the Celestial Quarters, yet the Celestial Quarters may be called the Horse Ancestor and are not truly the silkworm deity.

sentences.zh: 淮南子引蠶經，黃帝元妃西陵氏始蠶，其制衣裳自此始。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi cites the Silkworm Classic: the Yellow Emperor's primary consort Lady Xiling of Xiling first raised silkworms; from this the making of garments began.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi cites the Silkworm Classic: the Yellow Emperor's primary consort, Lady Xiling of Xiling, first raised silkworms, and from this the making of garments began.

sentences.zh: 漢祀菀窳婦人、寓氏公主，事本無稽。

translations.literal: The Han sacrificed to Lady Wanyu and Princess Yushi—matters without any basis in fact.
translations.idiomatic: The Han sacrificed to Lady Wanyu and Princess Yushi—traditions without historical foundation.

sentences.zh: 先蠶之名，禮經不載。

translations.literal: The name Spirit of the First Silkworm is not recorded in the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: The title Spirit of the First Silkworm appears in no ritual classic.

sentences.zh: 隋始有壇，建宮北三里，高四尺。

translations.literal: The Sui first had an altar, built a hall three li north of the palace, four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui first established an altar, building a hall three li north of the palace, four chi high.

sentences.zh: 唐會要，遣有司饗先蠶如先農。

translations.literal: The Tang Statistical Compendium records dispatching officials to feast the Spirit of the First Silkworm as with the Spirit of the First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Statistical Compendium records that officials were dispatched to offer to the Spirit of the First Silkworm according to the precedent for the Spirit of the First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 宋景德三年，命官攝祀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde of Song, officials were ordered to perform the sacrifice by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jingde era of Song, officials were ordered to perform the sacrifice by proxy.

sentences.zh: 有明釐正祀典，百神各依本號，如農始炎帝，止稱先農神，則蠶始黃帝，亦宜止稱先蠶神。

translations.literal: The Ming rectified the sacrificial canon: each spirit kept its proper title; as farming began with the Flame Emperor and is only called Spirit of the First Farmer, so since sericulture began with the Yellow Emperor it should only be called Spirit of the First Silkworm.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming rectified the sacrificial canon so that each deity kept its proper title: as farming began with the Flame Emperor and is addressed only as the Spirit of the First Farmer, so since sericulture began with the Yellow Emperor it should be addressed only as the Spirit of the First Silkworm.

sentences.zh: 按周制，蠶於北郊。

translations.literal: According to Zhou institutions, silkworms were worshipped at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: According to Zhou institutions, silkworm worship belonged at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 今京師建壇，亦北郊為宜。」

translations.literal: For the present, to build an altar in the capital, the northern suburb would also be appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: For the capital at present, establishing the altar in the northern suburb would be appropriate."

sentences.zh: 部議然之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated and approved.

sentences.zh: 侍郎圖理琛奏立先蠶祠安定門外，歲季春吉巳，遣太常卿祀以少牢。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Tulišen memorialized to establish a Spirit of the First Silkworm shrine outside Anding Gate; each year on an auspicious si day in late spring, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices would sacrifice with the lesser offering.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Tulišen memorialized to establish a shrine to the Spirit of the First Silkworm outside Anding Gate, with sacrifice each year on an auspicious si day in late spring by the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, using the lesser offering.

sentences.zh: 未及行。

translations.literal: Before it could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: This was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，始敕議親蠶典禮，議者以郊外道遠，且水源不通，無浴蠶所。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong, an edict first ordered deliberation on the ceremony of personally tending silkworms; deliberators argued that beyond the suburbs the road was far and water sources did not reach there, with no place for washing silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong, an edict first ordered deliberation on the ceremony of personally tending silkworms; deliberators argued that beyond the suburbs the distance was great, water sources did not reach there, and there was no place for washing the silkworms.

sentences.zh: 考唐、宋時后妃親蠶，多在宮苑中，明亦改建西苑。

translations.literal: Examining Tang and Song, when empresses and consorts personally tended silkworms it was mostly within palace gardens; the Ming also rebuilt it in the Western Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Examination showed that in Tang and Song, when empresses and consorts personally tended silkworms, the rite was usually held within palace gardens; the Ming likewise moved it to the Western Garden.

sentences.zh: 高宗鑒往制，允其議。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor, taking past institutions as his guide, approved their deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor, guided by past precedent, approved their proposal.

sentences.zh: 命所司相度，遂建壇苑東北隅。

translations.literal: He ordered the responsible offices to survey the site, and an altar was then built in the northeast corner of the garden.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the responsible offices to survey the site, and an altar was built in the northeast corner of the garden.

sentences.zh: 三面樹桑柘。

translations.literal: On three sides mulberry and paper-mulberry were planted.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry and paper-mulberry were planted on three sides.

sentences.zh: 壇東為觀桑台，前桑園，後親蠶門。

translations.literal: East of the altar was the mulberry-viewing platform; in front was the mulberry garden, behind the Gate of Personal Silkworm-Tending.
translations.idiomatic: East of the altar stood the Mulberry-Viewing Platform; before it lay the mulberry garden, and behind it the Gate of Personal Silkworm-Tending.

sentences.zh: 其內親蠶殿，後浴蠶池，池北為後殿。

translations.literal: Within was the Hall of Personal Silkworm-Tending; behind it the silkworm-washing pool; north of the pool was the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: Within stood the Hall of Personal Silkworm-Tending; behind it lay the silkworm-washing pool, and north of the pool was the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 宮左為蠶婦浴蠶河。

translations.literal: Left of the palace was the Silkworm Maidens' silkworm-washing stream.
translations.idiomatic: To the left of the palace ran the stream where silkworm maidens washed the cocoons.

sentences.zh: 南北木橋二，南橋東即先蠶神殿也。

translations.literal: Two wooden bridges north and south; east of the south bridge was the hall of the Spirit of the First Silkworm.
translations.idiomatic: Two wooden bridges spanned north and south; east of the south bridge stood the hall of the Spirit of the First Silkworm.

sentences.zh: 左曰蠶署，北橋東曰蠶所，皆符古制雲。

translations.literal: To the left was called the Silkworm Office; east of the north bridge was called the Silkworm Works—all conforming to ancient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: To the left stood the Silkworm Office; east of the north bridge stood the Silkworm Works—all in accord with ancient institutions.

sentences.zh: 是歲定皇后饗先蠶禮，立蠶室，豫奉先蠶西陵氏神位。

translations.literal: That year the empress's feast to the Spirit of the First Silkworm was fixed; a silkworm chamber was established and the spirit seat of the Spirit of the First Silkworm Lady Xiling was installed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empress's offering to the Spirit of the First Silkworm was fixed; a silkworm chamber was established, and the spirit seat of Lady Xiling, Spirit of the First Silkworm, was installed in advance.

sentences.zh: 屆日辰初刻，後禮服乘鳳輦出宮，至內壝左門降，入具服殿，妃、嬪從。

translations.literal: On the appointed day at the first quarter of the chen hour, the empress in ritual dress rode the phoenix carriage out of the palace; at the inner precinct's left gate she dismounted, entered the vestment hall, with imperial consorts and concubines following.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day at the first quarter of the chen hour, the empress in ritual dress rode the phoenix carriage out of the palace, dismounted at the inner precinct's left gate, and entered the vestment hall, followed by imperial consorts and concubines.

sentences.zh: 盥訖，升中階，就南階上拜位，六肅，三跪，三拜。

translations.literal: When ablutions were finished, she ascended the middle stair, took her place for obeisance on the south stair, performed six reverences, three kneelings, and three bows.
translations.idiomatic: When ablutions were finished, she ascended the middle stair, took her obeisance place on the south stair, performed six reverences, three kneelings, and three bows.

sentences.zh: 謝福胙禮三減一。

translations.literal: The rite of thanks for sacrificial meat was reduced by one of three.
translations.idiomatic: The thanksgiving for sacrificial meat was reduced by one step in the three-part form.

sentences.zh: 不讀祝。

translations.literal: The prayer was not read aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer was not read aloud.

sentences.zh: 爵三獻。

translations.literal: Three libation-cup presentations.
translations.idiomatic: Three libation-cup presentations were made.

sentences.zh: 凡拜跪，妃、嬪壇下皆行禮。

translations.literal: For all bows and kneelings, consorts and concubines below the altar all performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: For every bow and kneeling, consorts and concubines below the altar performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 餘如饗先農儀。

translations.literal: The rest was as at the offering to the Spirit of the First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the offering to the Spirit of the First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 禮成還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete she returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, she returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 越日，行躬桑禮。

translations.literal: On the following day, the rite of personally gathering mulberry was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she performed the rite of personally gathering mulberry leaves.

sentences.zh: 先是築台桑田北，置蠶母二人，蠶婦二十七人，蠶宮令、丞各一人承其事。

translations.literal: Earlier a platform was built north of the mulberry field, two silkworm matrons were appointed, twenty-seven silkworm maidens, and one director and one assistant of the Silkworm Office to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A platform had been built north of the mulberry field; two silkworm matrons, twenty-seven silkworm maidens, and one director and one assistant of the Silkworm Office were appointed to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 後散齋一日，從採桑妃、嬪以下畢齋。

translations.literal: The empress kept one day of scattered abstention; imperial consorts and concubines joining the mulberry gathering all completed abstention.
translations.idiomatic: The empress kept one day of scattered abstention, and the consorts and concubines joining the mulberry gathering completed their abstention as well.

sentences.zh: 是日昧爽，從桑侍班公主等祗候南門內。

translations.literal: That day at daybreak, princesses and others attending the mulberry service waited within the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: That day at daybreak, princesses and others attending the mulberry rite waited within the south gate.

sentences.zh: 巳初刻，後出宮，妃、嬪從，詣西苑，入具服殿。

translations.literal: At the first quarter of the si hour, the empress left the palace, consorts and concubines following, went to the Western Garden, and entered the vestment hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the first quarter of the si hour, the empress left the palace, followed by consorts and concubines, proceeded to the Western Garden, and entered the vestment hall.

sentences.zh: 傳贊分引妃、嬪、公主等就採桑位，典儀奏請後行禮。

translations.literal: The herald guided consorts, concubines, princesses and others in turn to the mulberry-gathering places; the master of ceremonies requested the empress to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Heralds guided the consorts, concubines, princesses, and others in turn to their mulberry-gathering positions, and the master of ceremonies invited the empress to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 出詣桑畦北正中，相儀二人，忌進筐、鉤，後右持鉤，左提筐，東行畦外。

translations.literal: She went out to the center north of the mulberry plot; two protocol officers presented basket and hook; the empress held the hook in her right hand and the basket in her left, walking east outside the plot.
translations.idiomatic: She went out to the center north of the mulberry plot, where two protocol officers presented a basket and a hook; the empress held the hook in her right hand and the basket in her left and walked east along the outside of the plot.

sentences.zh: 內監揚采旗，鳴金鼓，歌採桑辭，後東西三采畢，歌止。

translations.literal: Eunuchs raised mulberry-gathering banners, sounded gongs and drums, and sang mulberry-gathering verses; when the empress had gathered three times east and west it was finished and the singing stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs raised mulberry-gathering banners, sounded gongs and drums, and sang mulberry-gathering verses; when the empress had gathered three times to east and west, the singing ceased.

sentences.zh: 相儀忌受筐、鉤。

translations.literal: The protocol officers received the basket and hook.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol officers received the basket and hook.

sentences.zh: 後御觀桑台，以次妃、嬪、公主等五采，命婦九采。

translations.literal: The empress mounted the mulberry-viewing platform; in turn consorts, concubines, princesses and others gathered five times, and titled ladies nine times.
translations.idiomatic: The empress went to the Mulberry-Viewing Platform; in turn consorts, concubines, and princesses gathered five times each, and titled ladies nine times.

sentences.zh: 訖。

translations.literal: Finished.
translations.idiomatic: The gathering was finished.

sentences.zh: 蠶母北面跪，典儀舉筐授之，祗受退。

translations.literal: The silkworm matron knelt facing north; the master of ceremonies raised the basket and handed it to her; she reverently received it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The silkworm matron knelt facing north; the master of ceremonies raised the basket and handed it to her; she received it reverently and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 切之，授蠶婦，灑於箔。

translations.literal: She cut them and handed them to the silkworm maidens, who scattered them on the trays.
translations.idiomatic: She cut the leaves and handed them to the silkworm maidens, who scattered them on the trays.

sentences.zh: 後御繭館，傳贊引妃、嬪等行禮訖。

translations.literal: The empress mounted the cocoon hall; heralds guided consorts and concubines through the rite until finished.
translations.idiomatic: The empress went to the Cocoon Hall; heralds guided the consorts and concubines through the rite until it was complete.

sentences.zh: 還宮。

translations.literal: She returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 蠶事畢，蠶母、蠶婦擇繭貯筐以獻。

translations.literal: When silkworm work was complete, silkworm matrons and maidens selected cocoons, stored them in baskets, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When the silkworm work was finished, the silkworm matrons and maidens selected cocoons, stored them in baskets, and presented them as offerings.

sentences.zh: 卜吉行治繭禮，後復詣壇臨織室，繅三盆，手遂佈於蠶婦以終事。

translations.literal: An auspicious day was chosen for the cocoon-processing rite; the empress again went to the altar overlooking the weaving chamber, reeled three basins, and with her own hands distributed thread to the silkworm maidens to finish the work.
translations.idiomatic: An auspicious day was chosen for the cocoon-processing rite; the empress again went to the altar and the weaving chamber, reeled three basins of silk, and with her own hands distributed thread to the silkworm maidens to complete the work.

sentences.zh: 尋侍郎三德疏言：「親蠶典禮，為曠世鉅儀，請將壇址宮殿規制，興工告成日期，宣付史館。」

translations.literal: Soon Vice Minister Sande memorialized: "The ceremony of personally tending silkworms is a grand rite without parallel in an age; please order the altar site, palace halls, and their specifications, and the dates when construction began and was completed, to be announced and sent to the Historiography Institute."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Minister Sande memorialized: "The ceremony of personally tending silkworms is a rite of epochal magnitude; please order the altar site, palace buildings, and their specifications, together with the dates when construction began and was completed, to be recorded and sent to the Historiography Institute."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，始親蠶如儀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, personal silkworm-tending was first performed according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year, the empress first personally tended silkworms according to the prescribed rite.

sentences.zh: 尋定後不親蒞，遣妃代行。

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed that thereafter she would not attend in person and an imperial consort would perform by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon ordained that thereafter the empress would not attend in person and an imperial consort would perform the rite by proxy.

sentences.zh: 行禮階下，升降自東階。

translations.literal: The rite was performed below the stairs; ascent and descent were by the east stair.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was performed below the stairs, with ascent and descent by the east stair.

sentences.zh: 不飲福、受胙，不陪祀。

translations.literal: No drinking of blessing wine or receiving sacrificial meat; no collateral worshippers.
translations.idiomatic: There was no drinking of the blessing wine or receiving of sacrificial meat, and no collateral worshippers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，禮部請遣妃代祀。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Ministry of Rites requested dispatching a consort to sacrifice by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the Ministry of Rites requested that a consort perform the sacrifice by proxy.

sentences.zh: 時皇貴妃未正位中宮，帝諭曰：「妃所代，代後也。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial noble consort had not yet been installed as empress; the emperor issued an edict: "What a consort represents is representation of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial noble consort had not yet been formally invested as empress; the emperor issued an edict: "What a consort stands in for is the empress herself.

sentences.zh: 位未正，何代為？」

translations.literal: The position is not yet formal—what is there to represent?"
translations.idiomatic: The position is not yet formal—what is there to stand in for?"

sentences.zh: 因命內府大臣行禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered a grand minister of the Inner Court to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered a grand minister of the Inner Court to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 洎皇后冊立，始親饗。

translations.literal: When the empress was installed by investiture, she first personally offered.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress was formally invested, she personally performed the offering.

sentences.zh: 嗣後或躬親，或官攝，或妃代，並取旨行。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whether in person, by official proxy, or by consort proxy—all followed imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whether the empress attended in person, an official performed by proxy, or a consort stood in—each case followed imperial instruction.

sentences.zh: 其行省所祭，惟乾隆五十九年，定浙江軒轅黃帝廟蠶神暨杭、嘉、湖屬蠶神祠，歲祭列入祀典，祭器視先農。

translations.literal: As for what the provinces sacrifice, only in the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong was it fixed that at the Zhejiang Temple of the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan the silkworm spirit and silkworm-spirit shrines subordinate to Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou would have annual sacrifices listed in the sacrificial canon, with sacrificial vessels as for the Spirit of the First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: As for provincial sacrifices, only in the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong was it ordained that the silkworm deity at the Zhejiang Temple of the Yellow Emperor and the silkworm-deity shrines of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou would receive annual sacrifices listed in the sacrificial canon, with sacrificial vessels following the precedent for the Spirit of the First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 地祇順治初，定岳、鎮、海、瀆既配饗方澤，復建地祇壇，位天壇西，兼祀天下名山、大川。

translations.literal: Earth spirits: In the early Shunzhi era, it was fixed that the Five Sacred Peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and great rivers, having already been collateral spirits at the Square Pond, had an earth-spirits altar additionally built west of the Heaven Altar, jointly sacrificing to famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Earth spirits: In the early Shunzhi reign, the Five Sacred Peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and great rivers, already collateral spirits at the Square Pond, were given a separate earth-spirits altar west of the Heaven Altar, where famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm were also worshipped.

sentences.zh: 三年，定北鎮、北海合遣一人，東嶽、東鎮、東海一人，西嶽、西鎮、江瀆一人，中嶽、淮瀆、濟瀆一人，北嶽、中鎮、西海、河瀆一人，南鎮、南海一人，南嶽專遣一人，將行，先遣官致齋一日，二跪六拜，行三獻禮。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was fixed that the Northern Guardian Mountain and the North Sea should jointly dispatch one person; the Eastern Peak, Eastern Guardian Mountain, and East Sea one person; the Western Peak, Western Guardian Mountain, and Yangtze River Spirit one person; the Central Peak, Huai River Spirit, and Ji River Spirit one person; the Northern Peak, Central Guardian Mountain, West Sea, and Yellow River Spirit one person; the Southern Guardian Mountain and South Sea one person; and the Southern Peak alone one person. Before departure, an advance officer first observed one day of abstention, performed two kowtows and six prostrations, and conducted the three-presentation rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, dispatch was fixed as follows: one officer for the Northern Guardian Mountain and North Sea together; one for the Eastern Peak, Eastern Guardian Mountain, and East Sea; one for the Western Peak, Western Guardian Mountain, and Yangtze Spirit; one for the Central Peak, Huai Spirit, and Ji Spirit; one for the Northern Peak, Central Guardian Mountain, West Sea, and Yellow River Spirit; one for the Southern Guardian Mountain and South Sea; and one officer devoted solely to the Southern Peak. Before each mission set out, a preliminary officer observed a day of abstention, performed two kowtows and six prostrations, and carried out the three-presentation rite.

sentences.zh: 八年，封興京永陵山曰啟運，東京陵山曰積慶，福陵山曰天柱，昭陵山曰隆業，並列祀地壇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Mount Yongling at Xingjing was enfeoffed as Qiyun, Mount Dongjingling as Jiqing, Mount Fuling as Tianzhu, and Mount Zhaoling as Longye, all enrolled for collateral sacrifice at the Earth Spirits Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Yongling Mountain at Xingjing was titled Qiyun (Originating Fortune), Dongjingling Mountain Jiqing (Accumulated Blessing), Fuling Mountain Tianzhu (Heaven's Pillar), and Zhaoling Mountain Longye (Grand Achievement), and all were enrolled for collateral sacrifice at the Earth Spirits Altar.

sentences.zh: 十六年，徙東京陵祔興京，罷積慶山祀。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Dongjing tombs were transferred to be enshrined at Xingjing, and worship of Mount Jiqing was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the Dongjing tombs were moved to be enshrined at Xingjing, and sacrifice to Jiqing Mountain was abolished.

sentences.zh: 明年，用禮臣言，改祀北嶽於渾源。

translations.literal: The following year, acting on the ritual officials' recommendation, worship of the Northern Peak was moved to Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the advice of the ritual officials, sacrifice to the Northern Peak was relocated to Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，賜號鳳台山曰昌瑞，並祀之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, Mount Fengtai was granted the title Changrui and enrolled for sacrifice as well.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2, Fengtai Mountain was granted the title Changrui (Prosperous Auspiciousness) and added to the sacrificial rolls.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣祭如初制。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, dispatch for sacrifice reverted to the original arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, sacrificial dispatch returned to the original regulations.

sentences.zh: 惟南鎮、南海各分遣一人。

translations.literal: Only the Southern Guardian Mountain and the South Sea were each assigned a separate officer.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Southern Guardian Mountain and the South Sea each received a separate dispatched officer.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔封長白山神秩祀如五嶽。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict enfeoffed the spirit of Mount Changbai with rank and sacrifice equal to the Five Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, an edict enfeoffed the spirit of Mount Changbai with rank and sacrificial standing equal to the Five Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 自是歲時望祭無闕。

translations.literal: From then on, seasonal distant sacrifices were never omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter seasonal distant sacrifices were performed without fail.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，東巡祀泰岳，祝版不書御名。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, on the eastern tour he sacrificed at Mount Tai; the prayer board did not bear the emperor's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, on his eastern tour he sacrificed at Mount Tai; the prayer board omitted the emperor's personal name.

sentences.zh: 先一日致齋。

translations.literal: One day beforehand he observed abstention.
translations.idiomatic: He observed abstention on the day before.

sentences.zh: 太常齎祝版、香、帛、爵，有司備祭品牲薦。

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices carried the prayer board, incense, silks, and libation cups; the responsible officials prepared the sacrificial offerings, victims, and presentations.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices brought the prayer board, incense, silks, and libation cups, while the responsible officials prepared the offerings, victims, and presentations.

sentences.zh: 屆日衣龍袞，出行宮。

translations.literal: On the appointed day he donned dragon robes and left the traveling palace.
